spec.angle: GOV.UK, USWDS and CFPB for the frame, with Zerodha Varsity's chapter feel for lessons. Type does the work: one blue bar at the top, near-black headings on white, 1px rules, numbered lists, a contents list on long pages. The only boxes left hold a figure. Identity comes from the ledger, the badge and well-set type, not from colour blocks or decoration.
spec.thesis: Business Lab v5 is a white site at every OS setting: one #0B4AA2 bar across the top holds the badge and wordmark, a white strip of plain text links sits under it, text is near-black Atkinson Hyperlegible Next at 18-19px in a 640px column, and blue appears only in links, the one primary button per screen, focus rings and 4px 'you are here' bars. Lessons read like a textbook chapter (breadcrumbs, 'Lesson 1 of 4', a dated byline, a numbered Contents list, numbered sections), track pages become numbered step lists instead of the Academy cards, and every lesson, calculator, drill, check, dashboard figure and legal page stays word for word, with the ledger as the signature.

spec.typography: One family: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (Braille Institute, SIL OFL 1.1), already self-hosted as public/fonts/atkinson-latin.woff2 (34 KB, preloaded) and atkinson-latin-ext.woff2 (19 KB). The file is variable 200-800; @font-face keeps weight 400 700 and only 400 and 700 are used: 400 for reading and UI text, 700 for h1-h3, labels, nav, buttons, strong, ledger figures and table headers. No 600, no 800, no italics shipped. Its GSUB has tnum, so every figure, ledger, table, input and meta line sets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. It stays because it is the accessibility choice: I, l, 1 and O, 0 are distinct on cheap screens in bright light, which matters on a site made of figures, and it is not on the banned list. Setting headings in the body family at 700 is what GOV.UK (one family, bold headings), CFPB (Source Sans 3) and Varsity do. Bricolage Grotesque leaves the pages: delete its two @font-face rules in src/styles/fonts.css, the bricolage preload in BaseLayout.astro, --font-display and public/fonts/bricolage-latin.woff2 (41 KB) and bricolage-latin-ext.woff2 (19 KB). Reasons: no reference site uses a quirky display face; prototypicality predicts trust on bank and university sites (Miniukovich and Figl 2023, n=1,530; Tuch 2012); its 800-weight ink traps are what read as playful; NN/g advises at most two fonts and one is plainer; the 41 KB preload is the largest single request on slow 4G. Bricolage survives only at build time: the drawn B inside the badge (a path) and the share images (scripts/fonts TTF, via resvg), so readers download none of it. Kalam goes with the hand notes. Scale (360 to 1280): display 36-52 (home h1 only); h1 32-44, 700, line-height 1.1, tracking -0.01em; h2 24-32, 700, line-height 1.2, 48px above and 16px below (at least 1.5x more space above than below, USWDS); h3 20-24 (--text-lg), 700; lead 20-24, once per page; body 18-19 (Rello 2016 found comprehension rises up to 24px; GOV.UK body is 19px; NN/g found teens dislike tiny text); UI and small text 16; fine print 14. Reading text never drops below 18px and nothing drops below 14px. Seven sizes, never more than three in one view. Measure: p max-width 32em (about 70-74 characters) inside a 640px column; the old 64ch was about 90 characters because Atkinson's 0 is 0.648em wide. Line height 1.5 body, 1.35 UI and table cells. p margin 0 0 1em, li 0.5em. Headings text-wrap: balance, paragraphs text-wrap: pretty, sentence case everywhere, no letter-spacing on body. Hindi later: Noto Sans Devanagari 400/700 at the same sizes (Atkinson has no Devanagari), with the measure re-checked for that script.
spec.header: One <header class='site-header'> in two rows, static at every width (GOV.UK, USWDS and CFPB headers do not stick, and a static header can never hide focus). ROW 1, the blue bar (.site-bar): full width, background --blue, height --bar-h (56px below 900px, 64px from 900px), position relative, content in .container. The .on-band remap sits on the brand link and the Menu summary only. Left: the brand link (aria-label 'Business Lab home', min-height 44px): Logo at 32px, 12px gap, wordmark 'Business Lab' in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 700 at --text-lg (20px at 360, 24px at 1280), white, tracking 0, shown at every width. Right, below 900px only: details.nav-menu[data-disclosure]. Its summary reads 'Menu' (16px 700 white) followed by an 8px CSS border triangle; no border or fill, min 44x44, padding 0 12px, native marker removed; open, the triangle points up and a 4px white bar sits under the label. Its panel holds nav aria-label='Main': absolute under the bar (inset-inline 0, top 100%, z-index 45), white, 1px --border bottom, no shadow; six rows Learn, Calculators, Glossary, Dashboard, About, Search (plus Sign in when accounts are on), each 48px, --text-md 700 --blue, no underline, 1px --rule between, padding-inline var(--gutter); the current row is --ink with a 4px --blue left bar and aria-current='page'. From 900px details.nav-menu is display:none and the bar holds only the brand: Rajvir's 'blue heading'. ROW 2, the white strip (.site-strip): --bg, 1px --rule bottom, min-height --strip-h 48px, position relative, .container, flex. From 900px it holds nav.main-nav (aria-label 'Main') on the left: an inline list with 24px gaps, each link a 48px-tall box, 16px 700 --blue, no underline; hover gives a 2px --blue-dark underline at offset 4px; the current link is --ink with a 4px --blue bar along the bottom of its box, sitting on the strip's rule, and aria-current='page'. Below 900px nav.main-nav is display:none, so exactly one Main nav is ever in the accessibility tree and nothing is hidden (the .nav-wide rule that dropped Glossary and About is deleted). The edition menu (RegionTabs, class .region-tabs kept) is on the right from 900px and is the strip's only item below 900px. Summary: Flag 24x16 (2px radius), 8px gap, 'India edition' (or 'Choose an edition' on shared pages) in 16px 700 --ink, a 6px CSS triangle; 48px tall; no border, fill or pill; hover underlines the label. Its panel below 900px is absolute full width under the strip (details position static, anchored to .site-strip), white, 1px --border top and bottom, three 56px rows (flag 28x19, 12px gap, name at --text-md --ink, 1px --rule between); from 900px it is right-aligned, 280px wide, 1px --border, --radius, 48px rows. The current row is 700 with a 4px --blue left bar, aria-current (kept) and a CSS check at the right (the text glyph goes). Behaviour: both controls are native <details>, so they open with JS off and cause no layout shift. The RegionTabs script becomes one header script for every details[data-disclosure]: Escape closes the open one and returns focus to its summary, a click outside closes it, opening one closes the other. The lp:region write, data-edition-menu and the regionSub and regionSubs props (added by the calculator work) are kept. Focus: a 3px white outline at 2px offset inside the bar; a 3px --blue outline in the strip and the panels. Heights: 104px collapsed at 360 (56 + 48), 112px at 1280 (64 + 48). Width checks: at 360 the bar needs 16 + 32 + 12 + about 124 (wordmark) + about 94 (Menu) + 16 = about 294px; the strip's longest summary, 'United States edition', is about 215px. At 1280 the six links take about 500px and the edition summary about 200px inside the 960px container; at 900px they still fit in about 836px. Skip link stays the first focusable element (white, 2px --ink border, --radius, shown at top 12px on focus, targets #main).

Nav, rail, index, lesson-list, footer and edition links are link lists, never inside running text: no underline until hover. Nothing that is not a link is link blue. spec.darkMode: Removed entirely, with no neutral dark theme either. What Rajvir saw was not the design but the automatic dark token block, triggered by his Mac's setting, painting every page navy; removing it is the single change he will notice most. Evidence: light mode reads better for people with normal vision at every age and at night (NN/g summary of Piepenbrock 2013 and Dobres 2017: offer dark, never impose it); none of the reference sites ships one; a dark theme doubles every token, contrast pair and screenshot and forces the 'white in both modes' pinning workarounds, for a solo student maintainer; axe has never audited the dark theme because Playwright runs light only. Readers who need dark keep their browser's own force-dark and Windows forced-colours modes, which the site keeps supporting. How: (1) src/styles/tokens.css: :root { color-scheme: light }; delete '@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)', '@media (prefers-contrast: more) and (prefers-color-scheme: dark)', the dark series values and the .section-dark block; keep the light prefers-contrast: more block; reduce .on-band to the white remap. (2) src/styles/base.css: delete the dark a:hover rule. (3) src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro: <meta name='color-scheme' content='light'> and one <meta name='theme-color' content={site.themeColor}>, with themeColor '#0b4aa2' added to src/lib/site.ts (it matches manifest.webmanifest), so the dark theme-color and its raw hex #071a4a go. color-scheme light also stops a dark OS drawing native selects, radios, spinners, scrollbars and the dialog backdrop dark on white pages. (4) Delete every 'white in both modes' pin (--paper and --brand-navy on .doc, .video-ask, .edition-sum, .flashcard-front, .receipt, .btn-secondary, .cta-arrow, .pill-white, .course-thumb, the header nav and RegionTabs). (5) scripts/contrast-check.mjs: v5 pairs, light plus light+more only, on-band against :root --blue; the dark, dark+more and .section-dark markers are no longer read (today the script throws 'Missing ...' without them). (6) scripts/screenshots.mjs: schemes ['light'], widths 360, 768, 1280. (7) scripts/og-images.mjs: delete the unused dark slice. (8) src/pages/accessibility.astro: reword the 'light and dark mode' claim. (9) Docs and config listed in docsChanges; CLAUDE.md and .claude/* are Rajvir's edits. Forced-colors rules stay; no test sets colorScheme today, and a new test asserts the page stays white under a dark OS.

No ads, nothing to sell.' in --muted at 26px along the bottom. spec.motion: None as a design device. Removed: the cross-document @view-transition fade and its ::view-transition rules; html scroll-behavior: smooth (contents jumps are instant, as on GOV.UK and USWDS); the .btn hover scale(1.03) and :active scale(0.98); the .cta transforms; the tools summary chevron's rotate transition and every colour transition on buttons; all disclosure triangles change instantly. What remains: the consent switch knob slides over --dur-fast (150ms) under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and is instant otherwise; the global reduced-motion block stays as a safety net. No scroll-triggered effects, carousels, autoplay, skeleton shimmer, spinners or animated charts; loading states are text. State changes show as fill, border weight, text and aria attributes, never movement alone. Reasons: GOV.UK, USWDS, CFPB and Varsity use no ornamental motion; NN/g's young-adult research says interaction must serve the task; the brand already bans fade-ins.

whyProfessional: White pages, near-black text and one blue for the bar, links, the primary button and focus follow the shared pattern in docs/research/redesign-references.md (Varsity: 'one blue for links and the single button'; GOV.UK; CFPB's rule never to colour type unless it is a link; USWDS 'start in black and white'). Reber and Schwarz 1999: high-contrast text is judged true more often; Labrecque and Milne 2012 tie blue to competence.

A logo-only blue bar over a white strip of text links with a 4px current-page bar is GOV.UK's June 2025 header and service navigation, and it is literally Rajvir's 'blue heading and the rest of it's white'.

Removing the automatic dark theme follows NN/g's summary of Piepenbrock 2013 and Dobres 2017 (light reads better for normal vision; offer dark, never impose it) and removes the navy page Rajvir actually saw.

One family with 700 headings matches GOV.UK, Varsity and CFPB; none uses a quirky display face, and prototypicality predicts trust on bank and university sites (Miniukovich and Figl 2023, n=1,530; Tuch 2012). Dropping Bricolage also removes a 41 KB preload on slow 4G.
Body at 18-19px follows GOV.UK (19px) and Rello 2016 (comprehension rises up to 24px); NN/g found teens dislike tiny text as much as adults. Nothing drops below 14px.
A 640px column with p capped at 32em (about 70 characters) follows GOV.UK's two-thirds column and USWDS's 45-90 range, and fixes a measured bug: 64ch of Atkinson Next is about 90 characters.
Heading sizes capped at 44px inside and 52px on the home page match the references (GOV.UK 48, USWDS h1 40, CFPB h1 34); the old 60, 76 and 124px sizes made pages read as posters.

A numbered Contents list and numbered h2s in the markup, with a sticky left rail from 1024px, follow Varsity's '1.1' chapters, GOV.UK's contents-list research (5-8 items) and NN/g's table-of-contents advice (sticky only in a side rail, on the left). Numbers in the markup rather than CSS counters, as both judges required, so screen readers and search read them.

Track pages as a numbered step list with read-state circles follow GOV.UK step-by-step (tested with low digital literacy) and NN/g on cards (a poor fit for ordered, similar items); this is also Rajvir's 'ditch the Anthropic lesson design'.

The byline under each lesson title ('Reviewed ... · Written by ... · Checked by ...') and sources by publisher follow Stanford-Makovsky 2002 (updated +1.65, credentials +1.31, sourced +1.45) and Investopedia's 'Reviewed by / Fact checked by' block.
Underlined links, one solid 48px blue primary and outlined secondaries follow NN/g's flat-design eyetracking (weak signifiers cost 22% more time) and CFPB's 'avoid multiple primary buttons'.

Framed question blocks (graft from the Varsity proposal): on an all-white page a question with no edge blends into the prose, and a 1px frame helps a 15-year-old find what to answer without adding colour.

Removing blobs, stickers, hand notes, doodles and gold panels follows NN/g (decorative images are ignored, coloured boxes read as ads, teens reject childish visuals) and Stanford's 'design appropriate to the subject' (+1.21); design look drives 54.6% of credibility comments on finance sites (Fogg 2003).

The summary box, inset and details fold are USWDS's summary box and GOV.UK's inset and details; warning text for the fraud route is GOV.UK's warning text, firmer than a pale notice for content that matters in the first hour.
GOV.UK tables (no fill, 2px ink head rule, right-aligned tabular numbers) leave the ledger as the only distinctive data form: distinctiveness sits in the ledger, not the frame.
A two-way pager (graft) is the standard course pattern; a static 104px header on phones leaves more of the first screen for the caption, h1, lead and byline, where 57% of viewing time goes (NN/g).
A full-width bottom consent bar with equal Reject and Accept follows EDPB parity and Stanford (pop-ups -1.64); a visible On/Off beside each switch means state never rests on colour alone.
A 4px radius and square rules follow USWDS and GOV.UK; the 20px and 32px Aardvark and Ivy Kids shapes are what made the site read as a lifestyle brand.

Fixing the blank share cards matters because first impressions form in about 50ms (Lindgaard 2006), in chat previews too, and Stanford lists visible errors as the biggest amateur signal. A contact line in the footer (graft, shown once the address is real) scores +1.47 in the same study.
risks: Settled between the judges (look follows judge A, buildability and accessibility follow judge B): the Menu is a native <details> (B), not a script-revealed button, so no layout shift and it works with JS off; the consent island stays after the footer (B), because moving it first breaks the skip-link test at tests/e2e/a11y.spec.ts and the skip-link-first convention; section numbers are in the heading markup, not CSS counters (both); the lesson's 'In this track' list and the track page's 'Other tracks' come after the main content in the DOM (both), so the winner's sticky track list becomes a list beside the pager on wide screens; the badge recolour is a look call and follows A, but only with Rajvir's yes, so it ships unrecoloured; question blocks get a 1px frame (A); the banner reserves exactly its own measured height for scroll padding instead of 45vh (A on look, B on 2.4.11).

A concurrent session is building the seven new calculators and drill pages and has uncommitted edits to Header.astro, RegionTabs.astro, BaseLayout.astro, LessonLayout.astro, base.css, lesson.css, tools.css, regions.ts, og-images.mjs and more. Start only after that work is committed, branch from it, and re-read every file before editing. Its new classes (.field-note, .ledger-subtotal, .ledger-note, .index-meta, .tool-notes, .row-list, .tool-handoffs, .drill-scope, .rules-line, .tool-terms) and the regionSubs prop must be restyled and kept, not dropped.

Build coupling: scripts/contrast-check.mjs throws on any missing block marker (dark, dark+more, .on-band, .section-dark) and scripts/og-images.mjs throws without --field or --brand-gold inside npm run build. Rewrite contrast-check in the tokens commit; keep the old light tokens as plain hex (never var() aliases, which the hex regex cannot follow) until og-images reads the v5 names; then delete them behind a grep gate.

Token renames touch about 20 files; --font-display, --text-ui, --text-h3, --text-figure, --text-result, --radius-l, --line and the gold tokens are everywhere. The staged plan keeps pages rendering between steps, but mid-branch screenshots will look half-migrated.

Protected files: /privacy, /cookies and /terms change only through base.css (.eyebrow, .prose, .updated, .table, .table-wrap keep their names). A contents list there, the lp:activity row and the video lines are Rajvir's edits.

Standing docs and config encode the old look: BRAND_GUIDE v3.1, DESIGN v4.1, CLAUDE.md ('both appearances', 'light and dark'), .claude/skills/ship-check step 5 (pills, 20px radii, 'dark mode has no white boxes') and .claude/agents/design-reviewer checks 3-4. The reviewer will flag v5 until they change, and CLAUDE.md and .claude/* are Rajvir's to edit or approve in chat; no agent message can authorise it.
Dropping Bricolage from the pages removes the display voice Rajvir approved in v2; confirm with him. Share images keep it until an Atkinson TTF is approved, a small deliberate mismatch.

Readers who liked the automatic dark view lose it, including some low-vision readers; mitigation: /accessibility says the browser's own dark and forced-colours modes work, and the forced-colors rules stay.
/accessibility makes three claims that change (light and dark contrast, sticky header, 17px body); reword them in the same change.

The fixed consent banner can still cover part of the page on a first visit at 360x800; --banner-reserve must be measured, not guessed, and is only large (about 22rem) until the shorter copy is approved. Check by keyboard at 360x800.

The consent banner copy change and the footer contact line depend on Rajvir: the first is consent wording, the second shows only once site.contactEmail is a real address (today it is hello@business-lab.example).
SideNav.astro cannot render inside the Dashboard Preact island; the shared part is the .side-nav CSS, and Dashboard.tsx repeats the markup. Keep the two in step.

Moving the MDX body inside 'Show me' and rendering its ## headings as h3 (BodyHeading.astro) changes the outline, not the words; the three drill lessons without a worked example put the body inside 'Decide before you look'. Check the numbers and the Contents list agree on all 36 (a unit test and an e2e check cover it).

Removing the v1 branches assumes every lesson is v2 (all 36 are today); the layout must throw at build time on a v1 lesson rather than render it wrong. Removing the v1 schema fields is a separate content task.
Adding ProgressMarks to the lesson page makes 'In this track' show read marks; it must stay the page's only [data-review-line], with data-review-region on the article.

Body text at 18-19px and 48px h2 spacing make lessons about 10-15% longer; check the first screen at 360x800 still shows the caption, h1, lead and byline, and that no ledger figure overflows (a11y.spec 'never scrolls sideways').
--surface (1.08:1) and --tint (1.16:1) are nearly invisible without their edges; never drop the 1px rule. --link-visited is a cue only (1.20:1 against --blue).
Chart series-1 (#0c61c4) stays a second blue inside charts only; unifying it would need validate_palette.js re-run.
Without the recolour, the logo disc is 1.40:1 against the bar and relies on its white ring; the licensed badge may need a white one-colour header version.

Dead code goes in the same pass: region.report.stamp, the stat-primary on-field class, Blobs, Doodle, HandNote, TrackCard, src/lib/hand.ts, scripts/fonts/Kalam-*. No lockfile change is needed (the lockfile is protected).

final.summaryForOwner: The whole site becomes white in every setting, including your Mac's dark mode: the dark theme is gone, and that theme is what painted every page blue when you opened it in Chrome. The only blue block left is a bar at the top with the badge and 'Business Lab'; under it a white strip holds plain text links (Learn, Calculators, Glossary, Dashboard, About, Search) and the edition menu with its flag. Otherwise blue is used only for links, the one main button on a screen, the focus ring and a thin bar that marks where you are. Gold, the big rounded panels, stickers, hand-lettered notes, blobs, doodles and the Academy-style track cards are all removed. Everything is set in one typeface, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, with bold headings capped at about 44px and body text at 18-19px; Bricolage Grotesque goes, which also makes pages lighter on slow phones. Lessons read like a textbook chapter: breadcrumbs, 'Lesson 1 of 4', a line with the minutes, review date, author and checker, a numbered Contents list, then numbered sections such as '3. Show me', with the contents in a column on the left on a laptop. Track pages become a numbered step list whose circles fill in as you read, and question boxes get a thin frame so they are easy to spot. Every lesson, calculator, drill, check, the dashboard, glossary, search and legal pages stay with the same words, and the ledger with its double rule under the answer stays as the site's signature. This is what GOV.UK, CFPB and Zerodha Varsity share, and research on finance and education sites finds that looking like a trusted site of that kind is what earns trust. The first thing you will notice is a white page with a blue bar on top, even in dark mode, and larger, calmer text. Four things need your yes: shorter cookie-banner wording, recolouring the badge's blue to match the bar, adding an Atkinson font file so share images match the site, and the edits to CLAUDE.md and the reviewer and ship-check files; your real contact email will then appear in the footer by itself. The build starts on a new branch only after the calculator work in progress is committed, and nothing is pushed or merged: that stays your job.

verdicts.lens: Brand and owner skeptic: does v5 give Rajvir a white page with blue accents, no Academy look, no playful or template look, the same content, and a documented reason for every choice? Checked against the repo: the current track page source, commit b11be14, docs/research/redesign-references.md, src/lib/regions.ts, the lesson frontmatter, Logo.astro, the dark block in tokens.css, and the saved feedback notes. Contrast figures were computed with the WCAG formula.
problems: The Academy design comes back in another form. The spec's track page head is a caption 'Track 1 of 3', h1, lead, the meta line '4 lessons · 12 checks · about 34 minutes', a primary 'Start lesson 1' button, then ProgressMarks and 'Lessons'. That is the same sequence as today's course header from b11be14 in src/pages/[region]/learn/[track]/index.astro (eyebrow 'Track N · N lessons · N checks · N min', h1, lede, cta 'Start with lesson 1', ProgressMarks, then 'Lessons'), with only the thumbnail and panel taken away. Each track block on /[region]/learn keeps TrackCard's content in the same order (Track N, title, summary, lesson titles, the counts line). Rajvir asked to ditch that design, and what remains here is its structure.

The spec contradicts itself on blue headings. The --blue token says 'Never on headings, labels or figures', but /[region]/learn makes each track h2 (24-32px) a --blue link, /in, /eu and /us make each track h3 a --blue link, and the home page makes each edition h3 ('India edition') a --blue link.

There is still a lot of bold blue. On /in at 1280 I count about 35 bold blue runs: 6 strip links, 3 track headings, 12 lesson titles, up to 12 calculator titles (5 today plus the 7 being added), the button and other links, many of them at 20-24px (--text-lg 700). Every lesson also has 4-5 poll reveals and several Show me steps as 2px blue-outlined secondary buttons, and hint summaries in 700 blue. The footer has about 15 blue links on a blue-grey surface under a 4px blue rule. Rajvir asked for 'white with like blue accents'. This is blue everywhere again, as text and outlines.

The spec says 'one blue' but defines a family of eight: --blue #0b4aa2, --blue-dark #08357a, --link-visited #3d5a8a, --tint #e8eff9, --tint-rule #a9c2e6, --surface #f3f6fa (a blue-grey used for the footer, results bench, explorer, video poster and formula box), the logo disc #0C61C4 and series-1 #0c61c4. --tint with --tint-rule on every lesson's summary box is the 'baby blue' Rajvir rejected on 19 September. --link-visited is 1.20:1 against --blue, so it does not work as a visited cue; it only adds another blue. No reference site uses a blue-grey visited colour.

The logo will look wrong by default. The interim disc is #0C61C4 (Logo.astro line 27) on a #0B4AA2 bar, which is 1.40:1: two almost identical blues touching at the top left of every page. The spec leaves the recolour unapproved and ships that version, so the first thing Rajvir sees will look like a colour mistake. The disc is the stand-in drawn in this repo (BRAND_GUIDE section 4), so the decision should gate the header step, not trail after it.

The spec reads as a template. It copies GOV.UK Frontend almost part for part: a blue bar with the logo left and Menu right, a service-nav strip with a 4px current bar, a caption over the h1, breadcrumbs, inset text, warning text with a black '!' circle, details, step-by-step, GOV.UK tables and a bottom pager, all in one body font. It also removes the home hero ledger, so the first screen at 1280 (112px header, intro, edition list) has no ledger. That fails DESIGN.md section 0 ('crop out the logo and still know it's Business Lab'). On a money site that links to SEBI, FTC and CFPB, a government-service look also invites a wrong association.

More template repetition: the edition front at 1280 has tracks three across, then 32-44px stat figures three across (a 'three big numbers' band, even with sources), then 'What it covers' in two columns. The home 'How a lesson works' as numbered circles joined by a connector is the SaaS 'how it works 1-2-3-4' trope. The research notes say course pages are 'a list or a sidebar of units, each a line of text with a number'.
Read-state circles filling solid --blue come from no reference: GOV.UK step-by-step has no filled state. It adds blue discs and a game-like progress feel.

The lesson's first screen goes back on the tester's complaint ('too much text', 'didn't actually teach'; the 21 September notes say 'fewer parts before the point'). At 360 the page shows header 104px, breadcrumbs, a caption that repeats the breadcrumb's track name, h1, lead, a three-line meta line, 'After this you can' with three objectives, and an 8-row Contents list (about 380px). That is about 1,150-1,250px before '1. The document', so the lesson itself starts on screen two. The spec's own 57%-above-the-fold citation argues against this.

The byline makes a claim nobody stands behind. All 36 lessons have reviewedBy 'Business Lab editor', a role name for what was an agent editing pass, and PROJECT_BRIEF section 15 still lists 'Who reviews content for accuracy' as undecided. The spec moves this to the top of every lesson as 'Checked by Business Lab editor', copied from Investopedia's 'Fact checked by', which names real credentialed people. On a site whose thesis is 'work shown, nothing sold', that is a credibility claim with nothing behind it.

The evidence is not written down in the project. None of the cited studies (Miniukovich and Figl 2023 n=1,530, Tuch 2012, Piepenbrock 2013, Dobres 2017, Rello 2016, Stanford-Makovsky 2002, Fogg 2003, Labrecque and Milne 2012, Lindgaard 2006, Reber and Schwarz 1999) appears anywhere in docs/research. Miniukovich and Figl 2023 could not be checked. Rajvir's standing wish is that the work be research-based with sources on record.

Your progress stays on this device.' and the share-card foot 'Free. No ads, nothing to sell.' These are slogan-like fragments (anti-slop item 7).

verdicts.lens: Accessibility and engineering (contrast, focus, target size, reflow and zoom, JS budget, CSP, fonts, dark-theme removal, OG images and icons, e2e coverage, step size), checked against the working tree on branch interactive-tools, 2026-09-22
problems: P1 WCAG 2.4.11 fails in the header disclosures. Below 900px the Menu panel is 'absolute under the bar (top 100%)', so it covers the white strip. Tab from the last Menu link (Search) lands on the edition summary at y 56-104, which sits fully under the roughly 290px panel. The edition panel is 'absolute full width under the strip', so Tab from its last link lands on the breadcrumbs under it. The spec's header script closes only on Escape, an outside click or opening the other panel, never when focus leaves. With JS off the panels never close, which makes this a permanent failure, and the spec says both must work with JS off. Today's src/components/RegionTabs.astro .edition-list is also absolute, but only 240px wide; the full-width v5 panel is certain to overlap.

P2 WCAG 2.4.11 fails under the full-width fixed consent bar. html:has(.consent-banner){scroll-padding-bottom} moves only the root scroller. It cannot reveal a focused control inside a sticky box, because the box moves with the scroll. The v5 spec keeps three sticky boxes: the lesson Contents rail (from 1024px, max-height calc(100vh - 48px)), the calculator .results bench (from 900px, src/islands/tools.css:19) and the dashboard side nav (from 900px). At Playwright's own desktop size of 1280x720, the bench's Reset / Copy link / Share row sits at about y 570-620 on break-even, behind a banner about 150px tall. Today's banner is a 460px card on the right; the spec makes it cover every column.

P3 A single --banner-reserve 'measured at 360x800' is wrong at every other size. At 200% zoom (1280x800 becomes a 640x400 CSS viewport) the banner with today's copy is about 270px tall, and a 22rem (352px) scroll-padding-bottom leaves no snapport. The spec also sets the banner to 'no max-height'. At 400% zoom (320x256) a fixed banner taller than the viewport pushes Reject all and Accept all off screen, where they cannot be reached. The spec claims 200% zoom works but has no rule for short viewports.

P4 The spec drops test hooks and copy that the concurrent calculator work's e2e tests assert, and it says to branch from that work. tests/e2e/tools-foundation.spec.ts (untracked, in the working tree) checks: .taxonomy h2 'Tools that answer' and the exact .taxonomy-list a questions on in/eu/us; 'All 12 tools' / 'All 11 tools'; the home page .taxonomy-list with 5 links and their data-edition-path values; .tool-group h2 per moment in order; .tool-group a.index-row counts; .tool-jumps with #moving-out; .index-meta text; and '.crumb a' with the text '← All tools'. The spec replaces these with a flat '.index-list', h2 'Calculators', h1 'Calculators' and Breadcrumbs, and it deletes '.taxonomy' with the gold panel. Its copyChanges quote stale text ('Calculators that answer'); the tree says 'Tools that answer'. The home list and the tools index contain drills (job-offer-check, spot-the-fake), so 'Calculators' mislabels them. The proves for steps 7, 8 and 14 leave out tools-foundation.spec.ts and tests/e2e/tools/*.spec.ts.

P5 The protected legal pages depend on classes the spec does not list as kept. src/pages/privacy.astro, cookies.astro and terms.astro (blocked by .claude/hooks/protect-files.sh) use .section, .container, .column, .prose, .eyebrow, .lede, .updated, .table-wrap and .table. The keep list names only .eyebrow, .prose, .updated, .table and .table-wrap. The step 4 base.css rewrite ('lead paragraph', --column token, 'deleted: .stack, .section-alt, .section-tight...') could drop or rename .section, .column or .lede, and those pages cannot be edited to follow. cookies.astro's .table-wrap cannot get tabindex/role, so if its table ever overflows at 320-393px after body goes to 18-19px and --text-sm to 16px, axe scrollable-region-focusable (serious) fails, and the only fix would be a protected-file edit.

P6 The reflow and zoom claims are untested. playwright.config.ts runs 'mobile' as Pixel 5 (393px wide) and 'desktop' as Desktop Chrome (1280x720). Nothing runs at 360, at 320 (the WCAG 1.4.10 width) or at 200% zoom. The spec's '360' width sums, its 200% zoom claim, and /accessibility's 'axe-core via Playwright at 360px and 1280px' are all unverified. design.spec in step 21 adds no narrow-width or short-viewport check.

P7 The forced-colours claim is not supported for two background-drawn controls. The consent .switch (appearance:none; the track and knob are backgrounds, src/islands/consent.css) and the step-list read circle (a --blue fill) disappear under forced-colors:active, because backgrounds are replaced with Canvas. The spec says 'outlines and 4px bars are borders' but gives no forced-colors rules. The current-item bars must also be borders, not box-shadow (box-shadow is dropped in forced colours); the spec never says which.

P8 The skip link's focus ring is invisible. It 'shows at top 12px', which is inside the 56px --blue bar, and its 3px #0b4aa2 ring at 2px offset is drawn on #0b4aa2 (1.00:1). Today it is #0c61c4 on #0b4aa2 (1.2:1), so the defect exists already; v5 keeps it.

P9 Step 3 breaks focus visibility until step 5. It turns .on-band into the white remap (--focus #ffffff) while Header.astro still puts .on-band on the whole header, and the header's nav links sit on the white --paper pill group. The focus ring becomes white on white for steps 3-4. Today's gold ring there is already 1.7:1.

P10 The sticky results bench can grow taller than the viewport. With --text-h1 figures, 18-19px body and the ledger, the break-even and budget benches exceed 720px. A sticky box taller than the viewport keeps its bottom controls below the fold until the grid ends, so focus scrolling cannot reach them while the box is stuck. This exists today and the bigger type makes it worse.

P11 /accessibility's claim of 'at least a 44×44 pixel target' for buttons and links breaks. The new breadcrumbs (--text-sm inline, about 22px tall) and the rail's Contents rows (8px padding plus 16px x 1.35, about 38px) are under 44px. The spec rewords three claims on that page but not this one. Both pass WCAG 2.5.8 (24px, with spacing), so only the published statement is false.

P12 Steps 4, 11 and 12 are too big to review, and their proves only run subsets. Step 4 rewrites all 450 lines of base.css, removes a font and adds two components, but proves only the legal pages' axe tests, even though base.css restyles every page. Step 11 rewrites the 524-line LessonLayout.astro (v1 removal, numbering, the grid, the sticky rail, the pager, the track nav, ProgressMarks) and adds two new files and a test. Step 12 touches 12 components. A colour-contrast or overflow regression on pages outside a step's subset would go unseen until later.

P13 The logo claim is overstated. The badge's inner ring is stroke-width 1.5 in a 64 viewBox, which is 0.75px at the 32px header size. Anti-aliased at that width it does not deliver '8.35:1', and the disc is 1.40:1 against the bar. A logo is exempt from 1.4.11, but 'the white ring carries the edge' is not true at 32px.

P14 scripts/contrast-check.mjs is fragile in a way the step 3 rewrite must avoid. block(css, ':root') takes the first occurrence of ':root' in the file, comments included, and the token regex reads only 6-digit hex. A v5 header comment that mentions :root, or a 3-digit or var() value for any checked token, silently changes what is checked or throws.

Verified correct: every contrast figure in the tokens table (for example blue 8.35, 7.70 on --surface and 7.21 on --tint; border 4.21, 3.88 and 3.63; muted 7.62; link-visited 6.94; blue against ink-2 1.89). The dark-theme wiring is fully inventoried: tokens.css (both dark blocks), base.css:78, BaseLayout.astro:63-66, og-images.mjs:29 (an unused slice that does not throw if the block is missing), contrast-check.mjs:30 and :89, and screenshots.mjs schemes. No test sets colorScheme today. The share cards are blank: home.png, about.png and og-default.png all hash to e996dedb… The maskable icon uses #0B1240. atkinson-latin.woff2 is variable (wght 200-800) and has tnum in GSUB. The JS budget has headroom: the largest lesson page is 20.9 KB of 50 and the largest tool page 21.5 KB of 90. The CSP work adds no style attribute. All 36 lessons are template v2. Every file the plan names exists.

scores.angle: GOV.UK, USWDS and CFPB: design led by type, one blue bar, white service-nav strip, 1px rules, boxes only where a box holds a figure
scores.notes: This is the one an admissions reader or a teacher would take for a serious institution's site. White page, near-black #111418 ink, one blue, capped heading sizes (44px inner, 52px home), a caption over the h1, a meta line with 'Reviewed / Written by / Checked by', numbered h2s in the markup, and a left contents rail from 1024px. It matches Rajvir's words almost literally. The blue bar at 1280 holds only the badge and wordmark ('a blue heading'), and everything below it is white: nav in a white strip, footer on #f3f6fa, --tint only for selected states and the one summary box. The Academy TrackCard and .course-* CSS are removed outright. The phone header is clear: 'India edition' shows as words at 360, the nav is a real Menu button with a no-JS fallback, and there are 48px rows, an 18–19px body and 14px minimum fine print. It finds and fixes real bugs: 64ch in Atkinson is about 90 characters, the share cards are white-on-white and byte-identical, the .lesson-meta strict locator must stay unique, and contrast-check.mjs and og-images.mjs throw on the removed tokens. It is also honest about protected files and about CLAUDE.md and .claude/* being Rajvir's call. Weak points: (1) Risk of looking like a GOV.UK clone. The step-list circles, the '!' warning text, caption-above-h1 and a logo-only bar are Design System components a reviewer may recognise, and identity then rests on the ledger and badge alone. That is acceptable, but keep the ledger visible on the home page and edition fronts. (2) Polls lose their frame entirely. On a white page a question block with no edge blends into the prose; a 1px bordered question is clearer for 15-year-olds. (3) The consent banner has two filled primary buttons, which breaks its own one-primary-per-screen rule, and a 45vh bar with 45vh scroll padding is heavy at 360×800. (4) 'Both built from one steps array in the frontmatter' reads like a schema and content change to 36 lessons, which conflicts with 'content unchanged'. Derive the numbers in LessonLayout from the fields present. (5) One sloppy line ('--ink until hover? No: --blue') needs resolving. (6) It keeps the #0C61C4 disc on the #0B4AA2 bar at 1.40:1, so the header shows a slightly-wrong blue circle on blue. Still, it is the most complete and the most buildable spec, and every test hook is listed.

scores.angle: Zerodha Varsity and a clean textbook: one blue bar with inline nav, a 576px reading column, a module label with a thin blue underline, '1.1' numbered sections, ink-header tables
scores.notes: Serious and textbook-like. It is the best fit for India (Varsity is the reference Indian students already know), and the single-row blue bar with inline white nav is the most conventional header of the three. It deletes gold, panels, stickers, hand notes, blobs and the Academy cards, and keeps every feature. It measured Atkinson's advance (0.433em), so the 576px column really is about 70 characters. Better than the winner in small places: equal .btn-secondary 'Reject all' and 'Accept all' (no double primary), visible 'On/Off' text beside the consent switch, polls kept inside a 1px frame, a Previous/Next pager, a footer contact email, and the badge disc recoloured to the bar blue so the header mark reads as a white ring and B. Where it loses points: (1) The navy-filled table header rows (#0B1240 blocks) bring back exactly the dark-blue fills Rajvir complained about, and GOV.UK and CFPB avoid filled heads. (2) The '1.1' numbering comes from CSS counters plus per-order rules for .lesson[data-order=N] up to 9. That is hacky, screen readers announce ::before content inconsistently, and a lesson-number prefix implies reading order across lessons that are meant to stand alone. (3) Below 600px the edition trigger is a flag and a caret with the name only visually hidden, so a sighted phone reader loses the words 'India edition'. (4) The 16px UI text and 44px buttons are smaller than the winner's. (5) Recolouring the badge conflicts with BRAND_GUIDE §4 ('don't recolour it'), and Atkinson in the share images needs a TTF download. Both need Rajvir's OK. On a page it would look like a well-set course site; the dark table heads are the only thing that would still read as 'designed'.

scores.angle: Khan Academy course app crossed with a documentation site: units sidebar, white boxes with 1px borders, pale blue-wash surfaces, sticky header with hamburger
scores.notes: This one would look most like a template: a SaaS or Docusaurus starter rather than an institution. It builds boxes everywhere: home editions as three identical bordered boxes in a row, edition-front tracks as three boxes ('Track 1 · 4 lessons · 34 min' label, title, list, footer link), a hero with a card on the right, and dashboard boxes. The edition-front track boxes are the Academy course card Rajvir asked to ditch, minus the thumbnail. It also fills the footer, results bench, explorer, summary box, notice, video poster, review context and current sidebar rows with --blue-wash #F2F6FC, so pale blue creeps back over much of the page when he asked for white with blue accents. 'ul.checks' with CSS check bullets for 'Why Business Lab' is a landing-page feature-list tell. The fraud route 'If it happens to you' becomes a pale-blue notice rather than warning text, which is too soft for the content. Accessibility and clarity regress: the wordmark is hidden below 480px, so a phone reader sees only a badge, and small text drops to 15px and 13px. Its measure claim is wrong: 64ch in a 680px column at 18px is about 87 characters of Atkinson, not 60–68. It keeps navy --ink headings over a neutral --ink-2 body, a mismatched pair. What is good: the Khan-style units sidebar on track and lesson pages is familiar to students, the aside comes after main in DOM order (USWDS rule), there is a shared SideNav, and the 'Continue learning' button carries a 'Next: <title>' line. The spec is truncated after the glossary in the input, so components past that point went unscored.

scores.angle: GOV.UK, USWDS and CFPB: one blue bar with the logo, a white strip for the nav, black headings, rules and numbered lists
scores.notes: Contrast re-checked: blue on white 8.35, border 4.21 on white and 3.88 on the pale surface, muted 7.62, link-visited 6.94. The blue is 1.89 against ink-2, so every in-text link keeps its underline, as specified. The build coupling is named correctly: contrast-check.mjs throws on missing dark, dark+more, .on-band and .section-dark blocks, and og-images.mjs throws on missing --field and --brand-gold. The share images are white on white today; og-default, og/home and og/about share one MD5. The fix uses tokens by name and needs no new font download, because Bricolage stays at build time, and it adds a hash-diff assertion to og.spec. Removing the dark theme is fully costed: tokens, meta, site.themeColor (so no hex sits in a component), screenshots at light only, all three stale claims on the accessibility page, and the docs that are Rajvir's call. It is right that no test sets colorScheme. The badge is kept unrecoloured, per BRAND_GUIDE section 4. Every route is specified, including /review, /account, the legal pages, /404 and consent. The static header removes the risk that a sticky header hides focus. Other points: scroll-padding-bottom for the banner, 48px targets, text at 14px or larger, focusable table-wrap regions, heading numbers in the markup, and the :has([data-mark='read']:not([hidden])) rule, which works with the existing hidden toggle. Measure: the Atkinson zero is 0.648em (confirmed) and the average advance about 0.432em, so 32em is about 74 characters, close to the claim. Bricolage costs 41KB for the latin file (preloaded) plus 18.7KB for latin-ext; '60KB' counts both. Flaws: moving the consent island first breaks the skip-link test at a11y.spec line 65; the script-toggled Menu risks layout shift; 'steps array in the frontmatter' is ambiguous; and two filled primary buttons in the banner.

scores.angle: Zerodha Varsity textbook: one blue bar with the nav, a 576px column, numbered 1.1 sections, ink-headed tables
scores.notes: The contrast figures check out: rule-strong 4.80, ink-2 on blue-tint 11.24, white on ink 17.88, surface muted 7.62. Its measure is the most accurate: 576px at 19px is about 70 characters with the measured 0.432em advance. The 41KB Bricolage saving is correct for the preloaded file. The Menu and edition menu are native details, so they work with JS off and cause no layout shift. The rename map and grep list are explicit and every route is specified. Dark removal is costed step by step, and the accessibility page line 33 is caught. Costs and risks: recolouring the badge disc goes against BRAND_GUIDE section 4 and means rebuilding the icons; section numbers come from CSS counters in ::before with a data-order counter-reset hack, which screen readers and search handle inconsistently; share images depend on downloading an Atkinson TTF that needs approval; the theme-color hex stays in the layout; a fixed banner up to 60vh has no scroll-padding-bottom, a WCAG 2.4.11 risk; buttons are 44px rather than 48; and the text glyphs in 'Menu' and the caret are not marked aria-hidden. The filled ink table header is heavy against GOV.UK and CFPB practice.

scores.notes: Judged on the part received. The JSON stops partway through /glossary, so /search, /review, /account, the legal pages, /about, /write, /404, consent, the components, dark mode, logo, motion and keeps are not specified, and 'every route specified' fails. The contrast figures that were given check out: muted 6.88, border-strong 4.67 and 4.30 on the wash, on-blue-2 6.32 on the bar. Measure error: the 680px column at 18px holds about 87 characters with the measured average advance of 0.432em, not the 60 to 68 claimed, and 64ch (746px at 18px) is wider than the column, so it constrains nothing. It keeps 13px and 15px small text, hides the wordmark below 480px, and numbers sections with CSS counters. The Menu is a native details, which is good, and the width checks at 360 and 1080 are sound. Boxed edition and track cards plus blue-wash panels drift back towards the card look Rajvir rejected. An Atkinson TTF download is still pending approval.

proposals.typography: One family, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, sets everything: headings, body, UI, figures, the ledger and the wordmark. It stays self-hosted from public/fonts (atkinson-latin.woff2 33KB and atkinson-latin-ext.woff2 19KB, SIL OFL 1.1). The file carries a variable wght axis from 200 to 800; @font-face declares 400 700. Bricolage Grotesque leaves the site. Delete public/fonts/bricolage-latin.woff2 and bricolage-latin-ext.woff2, their @font-face blocks in src/styles/fonts.css, the bricolage preload in BaseLayout.astro and the --font-display token. That saves about 59KB and one preload on slow 4G, and the font budget drops to about 52KB of the 120KB allowed. Why Bricolage goes: (1) None of the references uses a display face. GOV.UK sets bold headings in GDS Transport, CFPB uses Source Sans 3 at 400/500/600, USWDS uses Public Sans, and Khan and Varsity use one sans each. Looking like the category is what predicts trust (Miniukovich and Figl 2023, 1,530 raters of banking and university pages; Tuch et al. 2012). (2) Bricolage's 96pt optical cut at 800, with ink traps and quirky terminals, is exactly what made headings read as editorial and playful, and that book-club register is being retired. (3) NN/g allows at most 2 fonts on a first screen, and one is plainer. Why Atkinson stays: the Braille Institute drew it for low-vision readers with distinct I/l/1 and O/0, which matters on a site whose content is figures. It also has tabular figures: the tnum feature is in the GSUB table of public/fonts/atkinson-latin.woff2 (checked), so the ledger keeps aligned columns with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Weights are 400 for reading and UI text and 700 for headings, labels, nav, buttons and figures. No 600 or 800, no italics shipped, and emphasis is by weight. Scale in px, 360 to 1280: display 34→48 (home and edition-front h1 only); h1 30→42; h2 24→30; h3 20→22; lead 19→21, once per page; body 18, up from 17, supported by Rello et al. CHI 2016 (gains to 24px), GOV.UK 19 and USWDS ≥16; ui 16; small 15; xs 13 (licence text and chart labels only); figure 30→40. Nothing anywhere exceeds 48px, matching GOV.UK, USWDS, CFPB, Varsity and Khan. Line heights: body 1.55 (within USWDS 1.5 to 1.62), lead 1.45, UI 1.4, h2 and h3 1.25, h1 1.15, display and figures 1.1. Tracking is -0.01em on h1 and display only and 0 elsewhere; body letter-spacing is never touched (MDPI Education Sciences 2023: small spacing changes cost reading speed). Measure: p max-width 64ch, and the reading column is 680px, about 60 to 68 characters at 18px (USWDS optimum 66; Dyson 55 to 75). Rhythm: h2 48px above and 12px below; h3 32px above and 8px below; p 16px below; li 8px, so there is at least 1.5 times more space above a heading than below it (USWDS). Headings are sentence case with text-wrap: balance; paragraphs use text-wrap: pretty; no ALL CAPS anywhere. Share images: resvg needs a TTF, so add scripts/fonts/AtkinsonHyperlegibleNext[wght].ttf and its OFL.txt. That download needs Rajvir's approval. Until then og-images.mjs may keep the Bricolage TTF, which is build-time only and never reaches readers.
proposals.header:
The header is the one blue block, identical on every page. It is header.site-header.on-band with background --blue #0B4AA2, no border or rule, and the white page meets its bottom edge. It is position: sticky; top: 0 from 900px and static below. The inner container is max-width 1080px with padding-inline --gutter.

AT 1280px (inline layout from 1100px) it is one 64px row (display flex, align-items center). From left to right:
(1) Brand link, aria-label 'Business Lab home', min-height 44px: badge 32px, a 12px gap, then the wordmark 'Business Lab' in Atkinson Next 700 20px/1, letter-spacing -0.01em, white.
(2) A 32px gap, then nav[aria-label=Main] ul with 4px gaps: Learn, Calculators, Glossary, Dashboard, About. Each link is 16px/700, white, no underline, padding 0 12px, height 64px (the full bar), display flex. Hover underlines it (2px, offset 6px). The current page (aria-current=page) gets a 4px white bar along the bottom edge from li a::after (position absolute; left 12px; right 12px; bottom 0; height 4px; background --on-blue).
(3) A flexible spacer.
(4) Search: a link to /search with a 20px drawn magnifier SVG (circle plus handle, stroke currentColor 2px, aria-hidden) and the text 'Search', 16px/700 white, min-height 44px, padding 0 12px, current bar as above on /search.
(5) A 16px gap, then the edition menu (RegionTabs, still a details element, class .region-tabs kept for tests). The summary shows a 24×16 flag, the short name ('India' | 'Europe' | 'United States') with a visually-hidden ' edition, change', and a CSS caret (6px border triangle, rotated 180deg when open). It is 16px/700 white, min-height 44px, padding 0 12px, 1px solid --on-blue-2 (6.32:1 on the bar), radius 4px, transparent. Hover and open states use background --blue-dark. On the home page, with no edition, it reads 'Choose an edition'.
The edition panel is absolute: right 0, top calc(100% + 8px), min-width 240px, white, 1px --border-strong border, radius 8px, 4px vertical padding, no shadow. Each row has the flag and full name at 16px --ink, min-height 48px, padding 0 16px, and background --blue-wash on hover. The current row (a[aria-current=true]) is 700 with a 4px --blue left bar (::before) and a CSS-drawn check at the right in --blue; the ✓ glyph goes.

AT 900–1099px the bar looks the same, but the five links and Search move into the Menu disclosure described below. Inline they would need about 983px, and only 852–1051px is available.

AT 360px (anything under 900px) the row is 56px min-height with 6px block padding. On the left is the badge (32px); the wordmark is hidden below 480px, and the link keeps its aria-label. On the right are the edition summary (flag, 'India', caret, 44px), an 8px gap, then Menu. Menu is details.nav-menu[data-menu]. Its summary shows 'Menu' and a three-bar icon drawn with pseudo-elements (three 2px white bars, 18px wide), 16px/700 white, 44px, 1px --on-blue-2 border, radius 4px. When open it reads 'Close', using the same label-swap trick as ShowMe. The open panel is absolute (left 0, right 0, top 100%), full width under the bar, white, with a 1px --border-strong bottom edge and z-index 45. It holds nav[aria-label=Main] with six rows (Learn, Calculators, Glossary, Dashboard, About, Search): each 18px/700 --ink, min-height 48px, padding 0 --gutter, 1px --border top divider. The current row has a 4px --blue left bar and a --blue-wash fill.

Used for poll reveals, 'Show line n', Reset, Copy link, Share, Reject/Accept all, 'Mark as read' and resume. .btn-link: no box, --blue text, underline thickness max(1px, .0625rem), offset .16em, min-height 44px, padding 0 4px; hover thickness 3px and --blue-dark. components.name: Links
components.spec: a: color --blue; text-decoration underline; thickness max(1px, .0625rem); text-underline-offset .16em. Hover: color --blue-dark, thickness max(3px, .1875rem, .12em) (GOV.UK). components.name: Inputs (text, number, email, search)
components.spec: Label above in 16px 700 --ink; hint between label and field in 15px --muted, tied with aria-describedby; error text in 15px 700 --error above the field with a visually-hidden 'Error:' prefix. Field: font 18px Atkinson, tabular-nums; min-height 48px; padding 10px 12px; 1px solid --border-strong; radius 4px; background --bg; color --ink; width 100% (max-width set per form). components.name: Select
components.spec: Same box as an input (48px, 1px --border-strong, radius 4px, 18px). appearance: auto, so the native control renders light because color-scheme is light, with padding-right 32px. Used for the edition filter on search and the currency pickers. No custom arrow image.

components.name: Radios, checkboxes, switch
components.spec: Radios and checkboxes use accent-color --blue, 20×20, with margin 0 inside option rows. The switch lives only in the consent dialog: see its spec. It is the one --radius-pill user.

components.name: Table (.table, lesson tables, tool tables, dashboard table)

No fills, no stripes (stripes only with more than 5 columns), no vertical rules. .table-wrap: overflow-x auto, tabindex=0, role=region and an aria-label naming the table (axe scrollable-region-focusable).

components.name: Ledger (.ledger, .ledger-row, .ledger-label, .ledger-figure, .ledger-total)

components.name: Show me (the stepped ledger)

components.name: Footer (src/components/Footer.astro)

The .section-dark class and its token remap are deleted; the Site column link reads 'Calculators'.

components.name: Focus ring
components.spec: :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; } on white and --blue-wash (8.35:1 / 7.70:1). Inside .on-band, --focus is #FFFFFF (8.35:1 on the bar). Inputs and selects use offset 0 and border-color --blue. Summary buttons and preset keys use the same ring. :target and :focus-visible keep scroll-margin-top calc(var(--header-h) + var(--space-5)) (WCAG 2.4.11), and html keeps scroll-padding-top from --header-h. components.name: Print

Body is 12pt --print-ink on --print-paper; boxes, the bench and notices get a 1px --print-line border and no fill. External links print their URL. components.name: Contrast gate (scripts/contrast-check.mjs)
components.spec: Rewrite the pairs table for v5 and fail below the minimum. On white: ink, ink-2, muted, blue, blue-dark, link-visited, error, success at 4.5; border-strong and focus at 3. On --blue-wash: ink, ink-2, muted, blue, error, success at 4.5; border-strong at 3. On --blue-tint: ink, muted, blue at 4.5. on-blue on blue and on blue-dark, and on-blue-2 on blue, at 4.5. .on-band block: ink, ink-2, muted and focus on #0B4AA2. More-contrast block: muted on bg at 7. Delete the dark, dark+more and .section-dark blocks and the markers that throw when those blocks are missing.

proposals.darkMode:
Removed entirely. The site has one light appearance and stays white whatever the OS setting. The navy page Rajvir saw was the automatic dark theme: his Mac is in dark mode, and tokens.css:8 declares color-scheme: light dark with a prefers-color-scheme: dark block that repaints about 40 tokens (--field #071a4a, --bg #101a4f, gold links and buttons).

Why not a neutral dark theme:
(1) The evidence favours light for normal-vision reading at every age and text size (Piepenbrock et al. 2013; Dobres et al. 2017; NN/g dark-mode review), and NN/g's advice is to offer dark as an opt-in, not impose it.
(2) The cost is real. Every pair is checked twice. Half of scripts/screenshots.mjs output is dark. There are 12 --paper/--brand-navy pinning points that exist only for dark. Axe has never audited dark, because the Playwright projects run light only.
(3) The owner's request is 'the entire page white with blue accents'.

Exact changes:
- src/styles/tokens.css: set :root color-scheme: light. Delete @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) and @media (prefers-contrast: more) and (prefers-color-scheme: dark). Keep the light more-contrast block and all forced-colors rules.
- src/styles/base.css: delete the dark a:hover rule.
- src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro: <meta name=color-scheme content=light>, and one theme-color #0b4aa2 with no media query (the dark #071a4a meta goes). Both color-scheme declarations are needed, or a dark OS draws native selects, radios, scrollbars, number spinners and the dialog in dark on a white page.
- Delete every 'white in both modes' pin: .doc, .video-ask, .course-thumb, .edition-sum, .flashcard-front, .receipt, .btn-secondary, .cta-arrow, .pill-white, header .main-nav, RegionTabs lists.
- scripts/contrast-check.mjs: drop the dark and dark+more loops and markers.
- scripts/screenshots.mjs: schemes becomes ['light'] plus one extra pass with colorScheme 'dark' saved as *_darkos.png. That pass must look identical to light, and proves the fix Rajvir asked for.
- Add one e2e test (tests/e2e/theme.spec.ts): with page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' }) on / and on a lesson, body background is rgb(255, 255, 255) and .site-header background is rgb(11, 74, 162).
- src/pages/accessibility.astro:33: reword (see pages).
- Docs: docs/BRAND_GUIDE.md §2 'Dark mode' and §8 item 9, docs/DESIGN.md §1, §2, §5 and §7 lose dark.

The 'both appearances' rule in CLAUDE.md, the ship-check skill step 5 ('dark mode has no white boxes') and design-reviewer check 4 must change too, but those are Rajvir's edits, not the builder's. If a reader later asks for dark, the answer is an explicit Appearance switch ([data-theme=dark]) in a neutral near-black with white text and the same one blue lightened for links, never navy and gold. That is not part of v5.
proposals.logo: Keep the interim club badge exactly as drawn in src/components/Logo.astro and scripts/brand-mark.mjs: the #0C61C4 disc, a thin white ring, and a white B outlined from Bricolage 800 as a path, so it needs no font. The brand guide §4 forbids recolouring, and the licensed file is still pending. Sizes: 32px in the header bar (was 40) and 32px in the footer, aria-hidden beside the wordmark, with the link labelled 'Business Lab home'. The wordmark 'Business Lab' changes from Bricolage 800 to Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 700, 20px, letter-spacing -0.01em: white (#FFFFFF, 8.35:1) on the bar and --ink in the footer. It is hidden below 480px in the header only. Known weakness: the #0C61C4 disc on the #0B4AA2 bar is only 1.40:1. At 32px the badge reads as a white B in a thin white ring on blue, which is acceptable because the wordmark names the site at ≥480px and the badge is decorative. When the licensed badge arrives, check it at 32px on #0B4AA2. If detail is lost, ask for the licensor's single-colour white version for dark backgrounds rather than inventing a recolour. Favicon, logo-mark.svg and the app and maskable icons are unchanged. Share images (scripts/og-images.mjs, which fixes today's white-on-white cards): a white 1200×630 card with a 112px --blue top band holding the 60px badge and the white wordmark; the page title in --ink bold at 64–78px from x=72; the edition and kind label in --muted; a 4px --blue rule above the foot line 'Free. No ads, nothing to sell.' in --muted. The script reads --blue, --ink and --muted from tokens.css and stops reading --field, --brand-gold and the raw #C2D4F0. tests/e2e/og.spec.ts gains an assertion that two different pages' images are not byte-identical.
proposals.motion: Almost none, and nothing that moves the page. Delete @view-transition { navigation: auto } and the ::view-transition-old/new rules (the cross-page fade), the .btn hover scale(1.03) and active scale(0.98), the .cta hover translate, and the edition caret's reliance on motion. The only motion left, all behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and all at --dur-fast 150ms with --ease: colour, background and border-colour transitions on links, buttons, nav and side-nav rows, answer-option rows and preset keys; the details triangle rotating 90deg and the edition caret 180deg; and scroll-behavior: smooth for the Contents list, the glossary A–Z and skip links. The global reduced-motion block (durations 0.01ms, no smooth scroll) stays. No scroll-triggered effects, no animated charts or ring, no skeleton shimmer, no auto-advancing anything. The dashboard clock updates as text with aria-live off. Evidence: NN/g's young-adult research (interactivity only where it serves a purpose, remove ornamental motion); brand guide §8.11 already bans fade-ins; Khan, GOV.UK, CFPB and Varsity pages load without page transitions.

Privacy posture: localStorage keys only, GPC as reject, learning time only after a yes, nothing sent

whyProfessional: White page with one blue for the header, links, the primary button and focus: CFPB's rule 'never use coloured type unless it's a link', GOV.UK's functional palette where each colour has one job, USWDS 'start in black and white', and NN/g's at most 4 colours on a first screen. Reber and Schwarz 1999 found high-contrast text on white is judged more true, so ink on white (13.7–17.9:1) is itself a credibility choice.

A blue header bar as the only colour block: GOV.UK's June 2025 header (one #1d70b8 bar on every page), Khan's navy header over a white page, and Rajvir's own words 'a blue heading and the rest of it's white'. The bar is identical on every page because GOV.UK's header guidance ties consistency to trust.

Plain text navigation with a 4px current-page bar: GOV.UK service navigation (5px bar in the link colour plus aria-current), USWDS header (left-justified, short labels, highlight the current section), and Varsity's six plain links. It replaces the pill group, which no reference uses.

Units sidebar with a 4px blue bar on the current item: USWDS side navigation (measured: bold ink plus a 4px left bar), Khan's course sidebar, and GOV.UK's step-by-step pattern shown as a sidebar on each content page, tested over 8 rounds with low-digital-literacy users.

Tracks and lessons as numbered lists, not Academy cards: NN/g's cards guidance (cards are a poor fit for ordered, similar, text-heavy items and take more space per item), GOV.UK step-by-step, and Varsity's numbered chapters. Cards survive only on the dashboard, where NN/g says mixed content suits them.

1px boxes, 4px and 8px radii, no 32px panels: USWDS radius 2/4/8px, CFPB 4px buttons, Khan's 1px-bordered exercise boxes. NN/g banner blindness: coloured blocks are skipped as ad-like, so the gold panels went and content sits in plain boxes.

Headings capped at 48px, a type scale of about 8 roles, one lead per page: GOV.UK (48 max, 80 exceptional), USWDS h1 40, CFPB h1 34, Varsity h1 32; NN/g visual hierarchy (few sizes, at most 2 large elements).

18px body at a 64ch measure in a 680px column: Rello, Pielot and Marcos CHI 2016 (comprehension rose up to 24px), GOV.UK 19px body in a 630px column, USWDS 66-character optimum, Dyson and Haselgrove 2001 (about 55 characters best for comprehension).

One family, Atkinson Next: GOV.UK, CFPB, USWDS, Khan and Varsity each use one sans. Prototypicality predicts trust on banking and university pages (Miniukovich and Figl 2023; Tuch et al. 2012). Wallace et al. 2022 found no single best font, so the choice rests on Atkinson's legibility design and its tabular figures.

Reviewed date, author and checker under the lesson title; sources by publisher at the foot: the Stanford-Makovsky 2002 credibility items (updated +1.65, author credentials +1.31, sourced +1.45, citations +1.30) and Investopedia's 'Reviewed by / Fact checked by' byline block, without Investopedia's ads.

Numbered Contents list under the lead and numbered section headings: GOV.UK's contents list (users strongly inclined to use contents links, 2021 research), NN/g's table-of-contents guidance (near the top, link text matching the headings), Varsity's '1.1 –' numbered H2s, and NN/g's layer-cake scanning pattern.

Underlined links and a solid blue primary button, one per screen: NN/g's flat-design eyetracking (weak signifiers cost 22% more time and 25% more fixations), NN/g link guidelines (colour plus underline, a visited state), CFPB (avoid several primary buttons; labels of 22 characters or fewer, hence 'Continue learning').

Summary box for objectives, inset for the key idea, GOV.UK details for the folds: USWDS summary box (3–5 key items, one per page), GOV.UK inset text and details. NN/g accordions: label by content, caret icon, never hide critical information, which matches the content guide's 'no check depends on the fold'.

GOV.UK-style tables with right-aligned tabular figures, and the ledger kept as the one signature: GOV.UK table and summary list, CFPB right-aligned quantities. Distinctiveness now lives in the content (the sum written like a cash book) rather than in the frame, which is where the prototypicality research says it should be.
No dark theme: NN/g's light-versus-dark review (light better for normal vision; offer dark, don't impose it) and the direct cause of Rajvir's complaint.

No stickers, hand-lettering, blobs or doodles: NN/g eyetracking shows decorative images are ignored and informative ones are studied. NN/g's teen research says teens reject childish content and expect informational sites to 'look simple and polished'.
A small, non-blocking consent box with equal Reject and Accept: Stanford 2002 (pop-ups −1.64, the second-worst item) and EDPB's 2023 cookie-banner taskforce on parity.

A pale footer under a 4px blue rule with the privacy, contact and licence links: GOV.UK (#f4f8fb plus a 10px brand rule) and CFPB (#f7f8f9 plus a 5px rule); Stanford 2002 (privacy policy +1.21, contact +1.47).
Every figure with its sentence and source; no stat banner, badges or awards: Stanford 2002 (sourced +1.45; award badges only +0.31) and the brand guide's anti-slop item 2.
No page fades or button lifts: NN/g's young-adult research (interaction only where it serves a purpose). None of the reference sites animates navigation.

Numbered headings use a CSS counter. Chrome and Safari expose ::before counter text to screen readers, but support is not universal, and body h2s from MDX break the count if one is missed. proposals.typography:
One family: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (Braille Institute, SIL OFL 1.1). It is already self-hosted as public/fonts/atkinson-latin.woff2 (34 KB) and atkinson-latin-ext.woff2 (19 KB). The subset is variable (wght 200–800), and its GSUB has tnum and pnum (checked), so tabular ledger figures need no second face. Keep the @font-face weight range 400 700 and use only 400 and 700. Preload only atkinson-latin.

Bricolage Grotesque leaves the page. Delete its two @font-face rules, its preload, --font-display and public/fonts/bricolage-*.woff2. That removes 41 KB from every first load on slow 4G. Reasons:
- Every reference sets headings in the body family at 600–700: GOV.UK (GDS Transport bold), Varsity, CFPB (Source Sans 3 at 400/500/600) and USWDS. No reference uses a quirky display face.
- Bricolage at 800, with its wide irregular forms, is what reads as playful.
- NN/g recommends at most 2 fonts; one family is the plainest textbook signal.

Atkinson stays because it is the accessibility choice: I/l/1 and O/0 are distinguishable on cheap screens in bright light, and it is not on the banned list. Kalam is deleted with HandNote. No Inter (Varsity's face), Roboto, Arial, Helvetica-as-brand, Space Grotesk, Geist, Instrument, Poppins or Montserrat. system-ui and Segoe UI remain as fallbacks only.

Scale: seven sizes, no more than three per view.
- 14px: fine print
- 16px: UI, meta and captions
- 19px: reading text, labels and inputs (GOV.UK body size; Rello 2016 found gains up to about 24px)
- 21–24px: lead, h3, ledger total, key idea, poll legend
- 24–30px: h2
- 32–44px: h1 and headline figures
- 36–48px: the home and edition-front h1 only. Every reference caps at 48px.

Rules:
- All headings are 700, sentence case, --ink, line-height 1.2 (h1 1.15), with text-wrap: balance.
- Letter-spacing is −0.01em on h1 and display only. Body text has no tracking.
- Paragraphs use text-wrap: pretty.
- Body is 19px/1.55 in --ink-2. Paragraphs have 1em below and list items 0.5em.
- Headings get 1.5× or more space above than below (USWDS): h2 48px above and 12px below; h3 32px above and 8px below.

Measure: the reading column is 36rem (576px). The average advance of Atkinson Next in lesson prose measures 0.433em (first-payslip body, weight 400), so 576px at 19px holds about 70 characters. That is inside USWDS's 45–90 and close to GOV.UK's 75 limit. Today's p max-width 64ch at 17px is about 705px, or about 96 characters, because ch is the '0' at 0.648em. Lead paragraphs get max-width 32em (about 70 characters at 24px).

Numbers:
- font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every ledger, table, figure, meta line and preset key.
- Lining figures by default.
- Section numbers (1.1, 1.2) are set in --muted 700 before the heading text.

UI text (nav, buttons, table headers, captions): 16px/1.35. Buttons and nav are 700.

Wordmark: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 700, 20px (18px below 600px), no tracking. White on the bar, ink in the footer.

Share images need Atkinson Hyperlegible Next Bold as a TTF in scripts/fonts, with its OFL.txt. It is used at build time only and never shipped to readers. Adding the file means a download, which needs Rajvir's OK.

components.name: buttons
components.spec:
.btn (primary, at most one per screen):
- inline-flex with an 8px gap; min-height 44px; padding 0 20px; 4px radius.
- 2px solid --blue border; background --blue; colour --on-blue (8.35:1); 16px 700; line-height 1.2.
- No transform and no hover scale.
- Hover and active: --blue-dark background and border (10.90:1).
- [disabled] or [aria-disabled=true]: --surface background, 2px --rule-strong border, --muted text (7.62:1), cursor not-allowed.
- Used for: Choose your edition, Start with the first lesson, Start with lesson 1, Continue: <lesson>, Play <n> min, Save choices, and the primary action of each sign-in step.

.btn-secondary:
- Background --bg, colour --blue, 1px solid --rule-strong border (4.80:1), padding 0 20px, 44px min height, 4px radius.
- Hover: --blue-tint background and --blue border.
- Used for poll reveals (Poll.astro: the summary class becomes 'btn btn-secondary'), Show line N, Reset, Copy link, Share, Mark as read, Reject all and Accept all, and Privacy choices.

.btn-sm: the same 44px floor, with padding 0 16px.
.btn-lg and .cta (label block plus arrow box) are deleted; their uses become .btn.

.btn-link: a text button in --blue with the link underline, min-height 44px, padding 0 4px. The '↗' ::after is deleted, as is .index-go's ' ↗'.

.btn-row: flex, wrap, 12px gap.

Labels are verbs in sentence case, 22 characters or fewer where the copy allows (CFPB).

components.name: links
components.spec:
Link styles:
- In text: colour --blue; text-decoration underline; thickness max(1px, .0625rem); text-underline-offset .16em.
- Hover: --blue-dark, with thickness max(3px, .1875rem, .12em) (GOV.UK).
- :visited → --link-visited #46557F, only inside .prose, .lesson-body, .lesson-fine and .note.
- Navigation and list links (header, menu panel, contents list, index rows, lesson rows, footer, sidebar) have no underline and are underlined on hover. They are standalone, never inside running text; the blue is 1.55:1 against body ink-2, so running-text links must keep their underline (WCAG 1.4.1).
- Headings, labels and figures are never link blue unless they are the link itself (an index title, an edition name).
- External links: rel='noopener noreferrer', no target=_blank, no arrow glyph.

components.name: inputs
components.spec:
input[type=text|email|number|search] and textarea:
- 19px (so iOS does not zoom); min-height 48px; padding 0 12px (textarea 12px).
- 2px solid --rule-strong border; 4px radius; background --bg; colour --ink; tabular-nums.
- Focus: outline 3px --blue, offset 2px.
- Invalid (aria-invalid=true): 2px --error border, plus the existing error text (16px 700 --error), tied by aria-describedby.

.field:
- The label is 19px 700 --ink above the input.
- The hint is 16px --muted, between the label and the input.
- 24px margin below.
- Number inputs max-width 16em; other fields fill the column.

Radios and checkboxes: 20px, accent-color --blue.

components.name: select
components.spec: select stays the native control (appearance: auto; it renders light because color-scheme is light). It uses the same box as the inputs: 48px min height, 2px --rule-strong border, 4px radius, 19px, padding 0 36px 0 12px. There is no custom arrow and no customizable-select styling (not Baseline). Used for currency in the calculators, the edition filter on /search, and year and region in sign-in.

components.name: table
components.spec:
Applies to .table, .lesson-body table, .tool table and .week-table table (Varsity's dark header row):
- border-collapse; width 100%.
- caption: 16px 700 --ink, left-aligned, 8px below.
- thead th: background --ink, colour --on-blue (17.88:1), 16px 700, padding 10px 12px, left-aligned (numeric columns right-aligned), no radius.
- td: 16px --ink-2, padding 10px 12px, 1px --rule bottom border, vertical-align top. Numeric cells are right-aligned with tabular-nums.
- No stripes and no vertical rules.

Wide tables sit in .table-wrap (overflow-x auto). Where the markup is not protected, add tabindex=0, role=region and aria-label so keyboard users can scroll them.

Print: the header fill drops to a 2px --print-ink bottom rule.

components.name: ledger
components.spec:
The signature; its structure is unchanged.
- .ledger-row: flex-wrap with 12px padding.
- Label on the left: 19px --ink-2. The step label is 700 --ink; the step sum is 16px --ink-2 tabular.

The key idea after it: p.key-idea is an inset with a 4px --blue left border, padding 4px 0 4px 16px, --text-lg 700 --ink. Remove class hl from its strong.

The nested details structure and the beforeprint open-all script are unchanged.

There is no panel fill.

components.name: edition menu
components.spec:
nav.region-tabs > details.edition-menu[data-edition-menu][data-disclosure]:

@media print:

components.name: headings and page rhythm
components.spec:
h1–h3 are Atkinson 700 --ink in sentence case. h1 is --text-h1 (--text-display on the home and edition fronts); h2 is --text-h2; h3 is --text-lg; h4 is 19px 700.
