Lesson section h2s carry CSS-counter numbers in --muted. Front-page sections are separated by --space-section, and fronts use 2px --ink rules over groups.

Nothing is centred except the account column.

.section padding is --space-section; .section-alt, .section-tight, .grid-3, .cluster, .stack, .display and .hairline are deleted as unused.

proposals.darkMode:
Dark mode is removed entirely, with no neutral dark theme. The white light theme already exists (screenshots/*_light.png). What Rajvir saw was the automatic dark token block, triggered by his Mac's dark setting, so this removal alone changes his view the most.

Why no neutral dark theme:
- NN/g's summary of Piepenbrock 2013 and Dobres 2017: light mode wins for readers with normal vision at every age and at night, and more so at small sizes.
- A neutral near-black theme would double the contrast pairs, the screenshots and the --paper pinning, and axe has never audited it: the Playwright projects run light only.
- The reference sites (GOV.UK, Varsity, CFPB) ship light only.
- Forced-colors and prefers-contrast: more give low-vision readers a better route.

Steps:
1. tokens.css: color-scheme: light on :root. Delete @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) and @media (prefers-contrast: more) and (prefers-color-scheme: dark). Keep the light prefers-contrast: more block with the new values. Delete the .section-dark and .on-band remap blocks.
2. base.css: delete the dark a:hover rule at line 78.
3. BaseLayout.astro: <meta name=color-scheme content=light>, one <meta name=theme-color content=#0b4aa2> with no media attribute, and delete the dark theme-color meta (raw hex #071a4a).
4. Delete every 'white in both modes' pin: --paper and --brand-navy overrides on .doc, .video-ask, .course-thumb, .edition-sum, .flashcard-front, .receipt, .btn-secondary, .cta-arrow, .pill-white, the header nav and RegionTabs.
5. scripts/contrast-check.mjs: drop the dark and dark+more blocks and the .on-band and .section-dark checks. Check these light pairs (plus more-contrast):
   - ink, ink-2, muted, blue, link-visited, error and success on bg
   - ink, ink-2, muted, blue and error on surface
   - ink, ink-2, muted and blue on blue-tint
   - on-blue on blue and on blue-dark
   - on-blue on ink (the table head)
   - rule-strong on bg (≥3)
   - blue as focus on bg (≥3)
   - on-blue as the header focus on blue (≥3)
6. scripts/screenshots.mjs: schemes ['light'].
7. scripts/og-images.mjs: delete the unused dark slice.
8. accessibility.astro:33: reword the 'light and dark mode' claim.
9. Rajvir's decision, not the builder's: BRAND_GUIDE §2 'Dark mode' and §8 item 9; DESIGN.md §1, §2, §5, §7; CLAUDE.md hard rule 'both appearances' and the workflow 'light and dark'; .claude/skills/ship-check step 5; .claude/agents/design-reviewer check 4.

Setting color-scheme to light in both the CSS and the meta also stops a dark OS from drawing native selects, radios, number spinners, scrollbars and the dialog backdrop dark on white pages.
proposals.logo:
The interim badge stays until the licensed club file arrives. Its disc is recoloured from #0C61C4 to the one blue #0B4AA2, in both src/components/Logo.astro and scripts/brand-mark.mjs (BLUE), which must stay identical. Then run node scripts/brand-icons.mjs to rewrite favicon.svg, logo-mark.svg and the app icons. The maskable icon's background changes from navy #0B1240 to #0B4AA2.

Contrast and placement:
- White B and ring on the disc: 8.35:1, up from 5.96.
- On the blue header, the disc merges with the bar, so the mark reads as the white ring plus white B. That is a one-colour logo on the brand bar, like GOV.UK's white crown on its blue header, and it ends today's 1.40:1 disc-on-band clash.
- On the pale footer the full disc shows, at 8.35:1 against --surface and 7.72:1 against white.
- Sizes: header 28px (below 600px) or 32px; footer 32px; favicon from the same drawing; minimum 24px.

Wordmark:
- 'Business Lab' in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 700, 20px (18px below 600px), no tracking.
- White on the bar, --ink in the footer.
- Live text, so it needs no font of its own. The Bricolage-drawn B inside the badge is a path and stays.

The logo appears only in the header and footer.

Share images (scripts/og-images.mjs), which also fixes today's white-on-white cards:
- 1200×630 on a white background.
- A 120px --blue top block with the badge and 'Business Lab' in white.
- The page title at 64px 700 --ink, wrapped to three lines, with the kind and edition label at 28px --muted.
- A 4px --blue rule above a 26px --muted foot line, 'Free. No ads, nothing to sell.'
- Colours are read from --blue, --ink and --muted.
- The font is Atkinson Next Bold TTF once added (OFL); until then Bricolage, at build time only.

Add an og.spec assertion that the home and about share images differ (distinct hashes), so this regression is caught.

When the licensed badge arrives, check a one-colour white version at 32px on the #0B4AA2 bar before swapping it in.
proposals.motion:
None as a design device:
- Delete @view-transition { navigation: auto } and its ::view-transition rules. GOV.UK, Varsity and CFPB have no page fades, and NN/g finds ornamental motion costs young adults efficiency.
- Delete the .btn hover scale(1.03) and :active scale(0.98), the .cta transforms, the tools '›' rotate transition and the colour transitions on buttons. State changes are instant.

What remains:
- html scroll-behavior: smooth for contents-list jumps, only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
- The consent switch thumb at 150ms under no-preference, as state feedback.
- The global reduce-motion block, kept.

No scroll reveals, carousels, autoplay, skeleton shimmer or spinners. Loading states are text (search status, 'Link copied.').
keeps: All 36 lessons on template v2, word for word, in v2 order: the moment and document, Watch, the body, Show me, Your turn, One more, Change one thing, What this means for you, Details, and three checks. Also Where this applies, the report route, Terms, Sources, the disclaimer and the licence notice.

The ledger as the only signature: label left, figure right, dotted leader, single rule above a total and double rule under the answer. It appears in Show me, Practice, EditionSum, calculator results and explorers, with maths from lesson-math and finance.ts.
EditionSum for each edition on the home and edition fronts
Five calculators in every edition (break-even, budget, savings, side-hustle, loan) with URL state, copy link, share, currency and lp:locale, plus India's 'UPI: spot the fake' drill
Inline explorers (margin, split, loan, growth, deduction) and drills in the lessons
HTML-first polls with radios and a details reveal, the :has() feedback rules, and everything working with JavaScript off
Drawn documents and made-up mock screens, with no real brands
Click-to-load video from youtube-nocookie behind the embeds consent, with a drawn poster and no third-party request before the reader says yes
Glossary, term popovers, #term-* and #pop-* ids, and the filter
Spaced review, /[region]/review, ProgressMarks (one per page), lp:progress and the wording without 'due'
Dashboard: every figure from this device, the week chart with its table, the ring, the track rows, the recent list, the timer, and Privacy choices via lp:open-consent
Pagefind search, with 'wasm-unsafe-eval' on /search only
Legal pages verbatim (privacy, cookies and terms stay protected), security.txt, the consent manager with GPC treated as no, and reject/accept parity
The account preview flow behind PUBLIC_ACCOUNTS_ENABLED, noindex while off
The edition menu on <details> with drawn flags, the lp:region write, and the Escape and outside-click close
The interim badge in the header and footer (until the licensed file), and the 'Business Lab' wordmark
Skip link, sticky header on wide screens, scroll margins for 2.4.11, and targets of at least 44px
The strict CSP: tokens only, no style attributes, no injected <style>, SHA-hashed inline scripts; no new islands and no JS-budget growth
Licence notice, rel=license and LearningResource and WebSite JSON-LD

Every test hook: .poll .opt .answer .fb .poll-status .return-line [data-return-line] .showme .showme-line '.showme-more > summary' .practice .practice-hint .steps .explorer .explorer-result .explorer-change .split-amount .video .video-poster-title .video-ask .drill-list .mock-screen .ms-from .ms-action .report .lesson-meta .lesson-fine [data-mark-read] [data-marked] [data-lesson-row] [data-mark] [data-review-line] data-review-region .stat .stat-source .results .result-figure-value .budget-row svg.growth-chart details.how .region-tabs summary '.region-tabs a[aria-current]' .consent-banner dialog.consent-dialog [data-consent][data-hydrated] [data-open-consent] .signin[data-hydrated] .preview-note .preview-code .r-title .r-excerpt mark [data-status] #edition #resume #resume-link data-edition-path
Sources and dates on every figure; stats with source links on the edition fronts; region.problems and region.note (the SEBI 30-day note)
Print styles and worksheet privacy, prefers-contrast: more (light) and forced-colors support
Flag.astro's raw hex, the one allowed exception besides the logo
The validated chart series palette (light values), with direct labels and a table on every chart
whyProfessional: White page with one blue for the header bar, links, the primary button and focus. This is the shared pattern of Zerodha Varsity, GOV.UK (the June 2025 blue header) and CFPB ('never use colored type, unless it's a link'). Miniukovich & Figl 2023 (1,530 participants) found that looking typical of the category predicts trust on bank sites more than aesthetics does.
No automatic dark theme. It is the root cause of the all-blue page Rajvir saw, and NN/g's summary of Piepenbrock 2013 and Dobres 2017 shows light mode reads better for normal vision at every age.

One family, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next at 700 for headings. GOV.UK and Varsity use a single family, and NN/g recommends at most two fonts. Wallace 2022 found no single best font but large costs from the wrong one, and Atkinson is built for disambiguation. Dropping Bricolage removes 41 KB from each first load for the slow-4G reader.

19px body in a 576px column, about 70 characters. This matches GOV.UK's 19px body and 630px column, Rello 2016 (readability rises up to 24px) and Dyson (about 55 characters is easiest). The measured Atkinson advance of 0.433em shows today's column runs about 96 characters.
Heading cap of 44px (48px on the fronts). GOV.UK, USWDS, CFPB and Varsity all top out at 48px or below; today's 60, 76 and 124px sizes are why the page reads as a poster rather than a course.

Module label with a thin blue underline, numbered sections (1.1, 1.2) and an 'On this page' list. This is the Varsity chapter pattern plus the GOV.UK contents list. It fits NN/g's layer-cake scanning (79% of readers scan) and its advice to place contents near the top and make it sticky only in a side rail.

Track and learn pages as numbered lists, not the Academy cards. NN/g says cards suit mixed content and hide order; GOV.UK step-by-step and USWDS side navigation mark the current item with a 4px bar. This also meets Rajvir's 'ditch the Anthropic lesson design'.

Reviewed date, author and sources in the lesson's top meta line. Stanford–Makovsky 2002 scores 'updated' +1.65, 'credentials' +1.31 and 'sourced' +1.45 for credibility, and Fogg 2003 found design look is 54.6% of credibility comments on finance sites.
Underlined links and a solid blue primary button. NN/g's flat-design eyetracking found weak signifiers cost 22% more time. The GOV.UK underline thickness and offset are copied exactly.
One small blue button per screen, with poll reveals and tool actions as outlined secondaries. This follows CFPB ('avoid multiple primary buttons') and the single small blue button on Varsity's home.
Tables with an ink header row, right-aligned tabular figures and thin rules. This is Varsity's table, with GOV.UK and CFPB's numeric alignment, and the ledger stays unfilled as the data signature.

Summary box and inset instead of gold notes, highlighter and panels. These are the USWDS summary box and GOV.UK inset text. NN/g's banner-blindness study found coloured blocks read as ads and are skipped (a right rail got 33× less attention than its size warrants).

No stickers, hand notes, blobs or doodles. NN/g eyetracking shows decorative images are ignored, and teens detest clutter and childish content (NN/g teen studies). The drawn documents and ledgers carry information and stay.
A footer on a pale ground with a blue top rule and a contact email. This is the GOV.UK and CFPB footer, and a contact email scores +1.47 for credibility (Stanford 2002).
The consent prompt as a non-blocking bottom bar with equal Reject and Accept buttons. Pop-ups score −1.64 for credibility (Stanford 2002), and the EDPB taskforce requires reject/accept parity.

A plain text-link header in the blue bar, with a Menu disclosure of full-width 48px rows on phones. This follows the GOV.UK header and service navigation and USWDS's left-justified short labels. NN/g teen research found small dropdowns hard, so every row is a large target.
No page fades or button lifts. Varsity, GOV.UK and CFPB use none, and NN/g finds young adults value interaction only when it serves the task.

Every page is headings, 1px rules and numbered lists, as on GOV.UK, USWDS and CFPB. The only boxes left hold a figure: a ledger, a calculator result, a dashboard number. proposals.typography: One family: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, self-hosted, SIL OFL 1.1, from the existing public/fonts/atkinson-latin(.woff2, -ext). The file is variable 200–800; the @font-face keeps weight 400 700. It has a tnum feature (checked in the GSUB table), so every figure, ledger, table and input sets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Weights are 400 for body and 700 for everything that must stand out: h1–h3, labels, nav, buttons, strong, ledger figures, table headers. There is no 600 or 800. It stays because it is the strongest accessible body face available: the Braille Institute designed it to tell I, l and 1 and O and 0 apart, it suits cheap screens in bright light, and it is not on the banned list. Using it for headings too is the GOV.UK approach (one family, bold headings); CFPB does the same with Source Sans 3. Bricolage Grotesque leaves the pages. Delete its two @font-face rules, the preload in BaseLayout and public/fonts/bricolage-*.woff2. That saves about 60KB, half the 120KB font budget, and one preload on slow 4G. None of the reference sites uses a quirky display face, and prototypicality predicts trust on finance and education sites (Miniukovich & Figl 2023; Tuch 2012). Its ink traps and changing widths read as playful at 60px and above, and at a 44px cap that character is wasted. It survives only at build time, in the drawn B of the badge and in the share images (scripts/fonts TTF via resvg), so readers download none of it. Kalam goes with the hand notes. Sizes: body --text-md, 18px at 360px and 19px from about 768px (GOV.UK sets body at 19px; Rello 2016 found comprehension improves up to 24px). The lead is --text-lg (20→24px), once per page. h1 is 32→44px at 700, line-height 1.1, tracking -0.01em. h2 is 24→32px at 700, line-height 1.2, 48px above and 16px below (USWDS: at least 1.5 times more space above than below). h3 is 20→24px at 700. Captions above an h1 are --text-md, 400, --muted. Small and UI text is 16px, fine print 14px, the home h1 36→52px. That is seven sizes in all, down from about fifteen, and never more than three in one view (NN/g). Reading text never drops below 18px. Measure: p is at most 32em (about 70 characters) and the reading column is 640px. Line height is 1.5 for body and 1.35 for UI and table cells. p has margin 0 0 1em, li 0.5em. Headings use text-wrap: balance, paragraphs text-wrap: pretty. Sentence case everywhere and no letter-spacing on body text. Hindi later: pair Noto Sans Devanagari 400/700 at the same sizes (Atkinson has no Devanagari).
proposals.header: One <header class="site-header"> in two rows. It is not sticky at any width (GOV.UK, USWDS and CFPB headers don't stick), and there is no pill group, gold or search box. ROW 1, the blue bar: full width, background --blue, class .on-band, min-height 56px below 900px and 64px from 900px, content in .container. Left: the brand link (accessible name 'Business Lab home', min-height 44px), with the badge at 32px, 12px gap, then the wordmark 'Business Lab' in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 700 at --text-lg (20px at 360, 24px at 1280), white, letter-spacing 0. The wordmark shows at every width. Right, below 900px only: a Menu button (<button class='menu-toggle' aria-controls='site-nav' aria-expanded='false' hidden>), un-hidden by the inline script only when JS runs. It shows 'Menu' in white, 16px 700, followed by an 8px CSS border triangle. No border or fill, min 44×44, padding 0 12px. Expanded: the triangle points up and a 4px white bar sits under the label. From 900px the bar holds only the brand, like GOV.UK's 62px logo-only bar. That is Rajvir's 'blue heading'. ROW 2, the white strip: background --bg, 1px --rule bottom border, .container, and it holds <nav id='site-nav' aria-label='Main'> and the edition menu (RegionTabs). AT 360: the strip is one 48px row, with the edition menu summary on the left: flag 24×16 (Flag.astro, 2px radius), 8px gap, 'India edition' (or 'Choose an edition' on shared pages) in 16px 700 --ink, then a CSS triangle. The summary is 48px tall; hover underlines the label. Opening it shows a panel positioned absolute at left 0, right 0 under the strip: white, 1px --border top and bottom, three rows 56px tall (flag 28×19, 12px gap, name at --text-md), 1px --rule between rows. The current row is 700 --ink with a 4px --blue left bar and aria-current. The existing Escape, outside-click and lp:region script is kept verbatim. With JS, the nav is collapsed (hidden) until Menu is pressed. It then renders above the edition row as a full-width list: six rows (Learn, Calculators, Glossary, Dashboard, About, Search, plus Sign in when accounts are on), each 48px tall, --text-md 700 --blue, no underline, 1px --rule between rows. The current row is --ink with a 4px --blue left bar, and aria-current='page'. Escape closes it and returns focus to the Menu button. Without JS the six links show inline in the strip, wrapping to two lines (16px 700, 44px tall, 16px column gap). Nothing is hidden at narrow widths, so the '.nav-wide' hiding of Glossary and About is deleted. Collapsed height at 360: 56 + 48 = 104px. AT 1280: the bar is 64px, with the brand in the 960px container and nothing else in the blue. The strip is 48px. On the left is the nav as an inline list with 24px gaps: each link is a 48px-tall box, 16px 700 --blue, no underline; hover gives a 2px underline at offset 4px in --blue-dark. The current link is --ink text with a 4px --blue bar along the bottom of its box, sitting on the strip's 1px rule, plus aria-current='page'. On the right is the edition menu summary (flag, 'India edition' 16px 700 --ink, triangle). Its panel is right-aligned under it: 280px wide, 1px --border, --radius, rows 48px, current row as above. The Menu button is display:none from 900px. Focus: inside the bar, a 3px white outline at 2px offset; in the strip, a 3px --blue outline at 2px offset. The consent island moves to the first child of <body> so it is first in tab order; the skip link follows it, then the header. Test hooks kept: '.region-tabs summary' stays visible at 393px (the Pixel 5 project) and '.region-tabs a[aria-current]' stays.

components.name: Buttons (.btn, .btn-secondary, .btn-sm, .btn-link)
components.spec: .btn is the primary button, one per screen: background --blue, white 700 label at --text-md, min-height 48px, padding 0 20px, --radius, border 2px solid --blue (so the edge shows in forced colours), line-height 1.2. Hover and active use --blue-dark for fill and border. Focus is a 3px --blue outline at 3px offset. Disabled gets opacity .5 and cursor not-allowed. There is no scale, lift, arrow box or shadow. .btn-secondary: white fill, --blue label, 2px --blue border, same size; hover adds a --tint fill and --blue-dark text and border. Use it for Reset, Copy link, Share, Mark as read, Privacy choices, every poll reveal (Poll.astro summary class changes from 'btn' to 'btn btn-secondary'), and the Show me steps. .btn-sm: 44px min-height, 0 16px padding, --text-sm. .btn-link is a text link: no fill or border, --blue, underlined, 44px min-height, inline-flex; the '↗' ::after is deleted. .btn-lg, .cta, .cta-label and .cta-arrow are deleted. Labels are verbs in sentence case, 22 characters or fewer where possible (CFPB).

components.name: Links
components.spec: a: colour --blue; text-decoration-thickness max(1px, .0625rem); text-underline-offset .16em. Hover: --blue-dark with thickness max(3px, .1875rem) (GOV.UK). Visited uses --link-visited only in .prose, .lesson-body, .lesson-fine and search results. Nav, rail, index, lesson-list, footer and edition links have no underline until hover, because they are link lists (NN/g). No link colour on non-links. No arrow glyphs on internal or external links. External links keep rel='noopener noreferrer'.

components.name: Inputs, labels, hints and errors
components.spec: text, email, number and search inputs and textarea: 2px solid --ink border, --radius, min-height 48px, padding 8px 12px, --text-md, --bg, tabular-nums. Focus: 3px --blue outline at offset 0, border unchanged. aria-invalid='true' gives a 2px --error border. The .field order is label (--text-md 700 --ink), then hint (--text-sm --muted), then error (.error, --text-sm 700 --error, with a visually hidden 'Error: ' prefix), then input, all tied by aria-describedby. Number inputs are max-width 14em; text and email are 100% up to 30em.

components.name: Select
components.spec: Same box as inputs (2px --ink, --radius, 48px). appearance: auto is kept; color-scheme: light makes the native popup light on a dark OS. The edition select on /search sits beside the search field from 640px.

components.name: Radios and the consent switch
components.spec: Radios use accent-color: var(--blue) at 24×24. The switch is kept as role='switch', 48×28, --radius-pill, track --border (off) or --blue (on), white 22px knob, which moves over --dur-fast (0 under reduced motion).

components.name: Table (.table, lesson tables, calculator year and amortisation tables, dashboard table)
components.spec: GOV.UK table. width 100%, border-collapse collapse, --text-sm, line-height --leading-ui. caption is left-aligned, 700, --text-md, 8px below. thead th: 700 --ink with a 2px --ink bottom border and no fill. td: 1px --rule bottom border. Padding is 12px 16px 12px 0, with no right padding on the last cell. vertical-align top. Numeric cells (.num, or the last column in tool tables) are right-aligned with tabular-nums. There are no stripes; CFPB stripes only above 5 columns. .table-wrap has overflow-x auto, tabindex='0', role='region' and aria-label from the caption, and a focus outline.

components.name: Ledger (.ledger and rows, EditionSum, Worked, ShowMe, results)
components.spec: Kept as the signature: label left, figure right, a 2px dotted --muted leader, a 1px --ink rule above the total, and a 3px double --ink rule under the final figure. The only changes: .ledger-figure uses --font-body 700 (was Bricolage) at --text-lg, and the total figure is --text-h2. Rows are 12px padding with 1px --rule separators in .steps and Show me. .is-loss stays --error. The wrap rules for long figures at 360px (WCAG 1.4.10) stay. Remove the .steps box border and the 12px radius; it sits on the page.

components.name: Poll (Poll.astro, the find-it question, practice, the three checks, Review)
components.spec: No card: .poll is margin 32px 0, padding 0, no fill. Checks are separated by a 1px --rule and 32px. .poll-label becomes a caption at --text-sm --muted ('Question 1 of 3'). The legend is --text-lg 700 --ink, 12px below. .opts is a grid with an 8px gap. .opt is a label row, min-height 48px, padding 8px 16px, white, 1px --border, --radius, with a 24px radio. Hover sets the border to --ink. Checked (:has) gives a 2px --blue border, --tint fill and 700 --ink text. The reveal summary is .btn .btn-secondary with the marker removed. .reveal-body gets a 4px --rule left border and padding 16px 0 16px 20px (GOV.UK details). .poll-status is 700: 'Correct.' in --success, 'Not quite.' in --ink, and the words carry the meaning. The @supports selector(:has(*)) feedback rules and the .fb/.answer markup are unchanged, as lessons.spec depends on them.

components.name: Document (Document.astro)
components.spec: A figure with 1px --border, --radius, white, 24px padding (16px at 360). No --paper or --brand-navy pinning; it uses ordinary tokens. .doc-head holds .doc-kind (--text-xs 700 --muted), .doc-title (--text-lg 700 --ink) and .doc-note (--text-xs --muted). Lines form a dl grid (label | right-aligned 700 tabular value) with a 1px dotted --border top rule per line. .doc-hint summary is --ink text with a 1px dotted --blue underline at offset 3px, preceded by a 6px CSS triangle, 44px min-height. The opened hint text has a 4px --rule left bar and 12px padding-left at --text-sm.

components.name: Show me (ShowMe.astro, ShowMeStep.astro)
components.spec: The ledger rows sit on the page. Each .showme-more > summary is styled like .btn-secondary .btn-sm and reads 'Show line 2', with 'of 5' in --muted 400. The '+' ::before is deleted. Once open, the summary turns into --text-sm --muted text ('Line 2 of 5') with no border, and it stays focusable. .showme-caption is --text-md --ink-2 on its own line. 'Show every line' is a .btn-link-styled button. The key idea after it is an inset (see Callouts). Hooks .showme, .showme-line, .showme-more > summary (text 'Show line 2', then 'Line 2') are unchanged.

components.name: Hints and details (practice hints, 'One more', the lesson details fold, 'How this is worked out', the dashboard table fold, doc hints)
components.spec: The GOV.UK details pattern. The summary is --blue --text-md 700, underlined, 44px min-height, preceded by a 7px CSS border triangle pointing right that rotates to point down when open (instant). The native marker is removed. The body has a 4px --rule left border and padding 16px 0 16px 20px. There is no panel fill. Practice hints read 'Hint 1 of 3, the method' and so on as now. Several can be open at once. Critical information never sits only in a fold (the existing content rule).

components.name: Video poster (Video.astro, VideoPlayer.tsx)
components.spec: A 16:9 frame with --surface fill, 1px --border and --radius. The poster head (top-left, 16px inset) is the title (--text-md 700 --ink) and the channel (--text-sm --muted). Centred is the Play button as a primary .btn with the drawn triangle glyph and 'Play 4 min'; the gold pill and its white border are gone. Bottom-left is 'Watch on YouTube' as a --text-sm --blue underlined link. The .video-ask panel inside the frame is white with 1px --border, --radius and 16px padding, --text-sm ink, and buttons .btn .btn-sm 'Choose, then play' and .btn-secondary .btn-sm 'Watch on YouTube instead'. The playing iframe fills the frame. The caption under it (.video-title 700, meta --muted) is unchanged. Nothing loads from YouTube before play and consent, and /cookies' 'still image with a play button' stays true. Hooks .video, .video-poster-title, /^Play/ and .video-ask are kept.

components.name: Callouts (inset, summary box, warning text, notification, note)
components.spec: .key-idea (inset, GOV.UK): a 4px --blue left border, padding 4px 0 4px 20px, margin 24px 0, --text-lg 700 --ink; .hl inside gets no background. .summary-box (USWDS, once per lesson, for 'What this means for you'): --tint fill, 1px --tint-rule, --radius, 24px padding. The numbered h2 sits inside at --text-lg, 8px below, then the three actions as a ul. .warning (GOV.UK warning text, for 'If it happens to you' on lessons, edition fronts and the drill): a grid of a 32px --ink circle with a white 700 '!' (aria-hidden) and the text in 700 --ink at --text-md, with a visually hidden 'Warning: ' prefix. .notification (the /account preview): a 4px --blue left bar, --tint fill, 12px 16px padding. .note: --text-sm --muted under a 1px --rule with 16px padding-top. .callout (the gold sticky note) is deleted.

components.name: Cards (only where a card holds a figure)
components.spec: .box: white, 1px --rule, --radius, 24px padding (16px at 360). .box-surface: the same with --surface fill. Allowed uses only: the worked-example EditionSum on edition fronts, the calculator results bench (.box-surface), the explorer (.box-surface), the five dashboard sections, the sign-in card and the consent dialog. Delete .card, .card-outline, .panel*, .sheet, .page-sheet, .grid-table, .pill*, .sticker*, .hand*, .doodle, .blobs, .grid-3, .cluster, .stack, .display, .hairline, .section-alt, .section-tight and .mega, along with Blobs.astro, Doodle.astro, HandNote.astro, src/lib/hand.ts, scripts/fonts/Kalam-* and TrackCard.astro.

components.name: Lists (index-list, lesson-list, step-list, contents, link lists, bullets)
components.spec: .index-list: ruled rows (1px --rule top and bottom), each a whole-row link: .index-title at --text-lg 700 --blue (underline on hover), .index-sub at --text-sm --muted, 16px vertical padding. .index-go is deleted. .lesson-list: a 32px number column (--muted 700 tabular), the title link at --text-lg 700 --blue (--text-md in .is-compact), summary --text-md, marks --text-sm; [data-lesson-row] and [data-mark] are unchanged. .step-list (track page and home steps): 32px circles with a 1px --ink border and a bold numeral, a 1px --rule connector drawn by li::before from circle to circle; read rows fill the circle --blue with a white numeral via :has([data-mark='read']:not([hidden])). Contents lists: ol, --text-md links, 44px rows, no bullets. Prose ul/ol keep disc and decimal markers with padding-left 24px and li margin 0.5em.

components.name: Breadcrumbs and caption
components.spec: Breadcrumbs.astro: <nav aria-label='Breadcrumb'><ol> at --text-sm, --ink links underlined (GOV.UK), with an 7px rotated-border chevron separator in --muted between items. The current page is not listed. 24px below. proposals.darkMode: Removed entirely. There is no neutral dark theme either: the cost is too high for what it gives. The evidence favours light for readers with normal vision in every measure tested (Piepenbrock 2013; Dobres 2017; NN/g: offer dark, never impose it). What Rajvir saw was not the design but the OS setting repainting every page navy. A dark theme doubles every token, contrast pair and screenshot, and it forces the --paper pinning workarounds, all for a solo student maintainer. Readers who need dark still have their browser's own force-dark and forced-colours (Windows High Contrast) modes, which the site keeps supporting. How: (1) tokens.css: set :root { color-scheme: light } and delete the '@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)' block, the '(prefers-contrast: more) and (prefers-color-scheme: dark)' block and the .section-dark block. Keep the light '@media (prefers-contrast: more)' block (--muted #33373d, --rule #6b7079). Reduce .on-band to the white remap for the bar. (2) base.css: delete '@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { a:hover … }'. (3) BaseLayout.astro: set <meta name='color-scheme' content='light'> and use one theme-color from site.themeColor (#0b4aa2). The dark theme-color meta and raw hex go. (4) Delete every 'white in both modes' pin: --paper and --brand-navy overrides on .doc, .video-ask, .edition-sum, .flashcard-front, .receipt, .btn-secondary, .cta-arrow, .pill-white, the header nav and RegionTabs. (5) scripts/contrast-check.mjs: rewrite the pairs for the v5 token names and delete the dark and dark+more loops and their block() markers, or it throws 'Missing …' and fails ship-check. Keep the light+more check (muted ≥7:1). Replace the .on-band check with white on --blue for text, focus and wordmark, and drop the .section-dark check. (6) scripts/screenshots.mjs: schemes ['light'] only (32 files, not 64). Consider adding 768px. (7) scripts/og-images.mjs: delete the unused `dark` slice. (8) /accessibility line 33: reword as listed under pages. (9) Docs and config: BRAND_GUIDE §2 'Dark mode' and §8 item 9, DESIGN.md §1, §2, §5 and §7, CLAUDE.md ('both appearances', 'light and dark'), .claude/skills/ship-check step 5 and .claude/agents/design-reviewer checks 3–4 must drop dark mode. CLAUDE.md and .claude/* are Rajvir's call. Tests: nothing in tests/ sets colorScheme, so no test changes. forced-colors rules stay.
proposals.logo: The interim badge is unchanged in drawing and hex: a #0C61C4 disc, a 1.5px white inner ring and the white B cut from Bricolage 800 (Logo.astro and scripts/brand-mark.mjs stay identical). Header: 32px on the --blue bar. The disc against the bar is only 1.40:1, but the white ring (8.35:1 on the bar) and the white B carry the edge, so the mark reads. Footer: 32px on --surface. The wordmark is Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 700 at --text-lg with letter-spacing 0: white on the bar, --ink in the footer. The brand guide's 'Bricolage 800 wordmark' line changes to match. Favicon and app icons are unchanged. The maskable icon's background in scripts/brand-icons.mjs changes from navy #0B1240 to #0B4AA2 to match the bar. The manifest already has theme_color #0b4aa2 and a white background. Share images (scripts/og-images.mjs) are fixed and redrawn to match the site. Today every card is the badge on white with white text, so the title is invisible, and home.png, about.png and og-default.png have identical md5 hashes. New card, 1200×630: a white background; a 96px --blue bar across the top with the 60px badge and 'Business Lab' in white; the title in --ink at 58–78px, 700, left at x 72; the label line ('Lesson · India edition') and 'Free. No ads, nothing to sell.' in --muted at 26px along the bottom; a 1px --rule above them. Colours are read from tokens.css by name: blue, ink, muted, rule, bg. No #FFFFFF or #C2D4F0 literals and no --field or --brand-gold. The Bricolage TTF in scripts/fonts stays as the card face because resvg needs a TTF and readers never download it. Add to tests/e2e/og.spec.ts an assertion that og-default.png and og/home.png differ by hash, so a blank card fails. When the licensed badge arrives (BRAND_GUIDE §4), check it at 32px on the blue bar. If it is mostly blue, it needs the simplified white-disc header version the guide already anticipates.
proposals.motion: None, except the consent switch knob, which slides over 150ms and drops to 0 under reduced motion. Removed: the cross-document @view-transition fade and its ::view-transition rules; the .btn and .cta hover scale and the translate on press; html scroll-behavior: smooth (in-page jumps are instant, as on GOV.UK and USWDS); the rotate transition on details markers (the triangle changes instantly); colour transitions on buttons. The global prefers-reduced-motion block stays as a safety net. There are no scroll-triggered effects, no loading shimmer and no animated charts. State changes are shown by fill, border weight, text and aria attributes, never by movement. Reasons: GOV.UK, USWDS and CFPB use no ornamental motion; NN/g's young-adult research says interactivity must serve a purpose; and the brand's own rule already bans fade-ins.

Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, self-hosted, now the only web font
The 4px spacing grid, the validated chart series palette in fixed order, data tables for every chart, print tokens
